cohensKappa.outcome: Measure agreement between two categorical raters beyond chance.
cohensKappa.typicalQuestion: Do measurements, raters, items, or methods agree reliably?
cohensKappa.resultMeaning: Reliability/agreement coefficient, uncertainty, and/or diagnostic performance.

diagnosticTesting.outcome: Evaluate diagnostic-test performance such as sensitivity, specificity and predictive values.
diagnosticTesting.typicalQuestion: Do measurements, raters, items, or methods agree reliably?
diagnosticTesting.resultMeaning: Reliability/agreement coefficient, uncertainty, and/or diagnostic performance.

fleissKappaUpd.outcome: Measure agreement among multiple categorical raters beyond chance.
fleissKappaUpd.typicalQuestion: Do measurements, raters, items, or methods agree reliably?
fleissKappaUpd.resultMeaning: Reliability/agreement coefficient, uncertainty, and/or diagnostic performance.

intraClassCorrelationCoefficients.outcome: Quantify reliability/agreement for continuous measurements or ratings.
intraClassCorrelationCoefficients.typicalQuestion: Do measurements, raters, items, or methods agree reliably?
intraClassCorrelationCoefficients.resultMeaning: Reliability/agreement coefficient, uncertainty, and/or diagnostic performance.

reliabilityAnalysisCronbachsAlpha.outcome: Measures the internal-consistency reliability of a multi-item scale (e.g. survey items intended to measure one construct).
reliabilityAnalysisCronbachsAlpha.typicalQuestion: Do my scale/survey items reliably measure the same underlying construct?
reliabilityAnalysisCronbachsAlpha.mainAssumptions: Items intended to measure a single underlying construct; items on comparable scales
reliabilityAnalysisCronbachsAlpha.resultMeaning: Cronbach's alpha coefficient (0-1) indicating internal consistency, plus item-level statistics (e.g. alpha-if-item-deleted) to flag weak items.

reliabilityAnalysisMcDonaldsOmega.outcome: Assess internal consistency using McDonald's omega.
reliabilityAnalysisMcDonaldsOmega.typicalQuestion: Do measurements, raters, items, or methods agree reliably?
reliabilityAnalysisMcDonaldsOmega.resultMeaning: Reliability/agreement coefficient, uncertainty, and/or diagnostic performance.

BlandAltman.outcome: Plots the difference between two paired measurements against their mean, to visualize agreement and detect systematic bias or trends across the measurement range.
BlandAltman.typicalQuestion: Do two measurement methods/observers agree, and does their disagreement change across the range of values?
BlandAltman.mainAssumptions: Paired measurements on the same subjects; differences approximately constant variance across the range (checked visually)
BlandAltman.resultMeaning: A scatterplot of difference vs. mean with a mean-difference line and agreement limits (typically ±1.96 SD), showing bias and the range of disagreement.

agostino.outcome: Test whether sample skewness differs from normality expectation.

ANCOVA.outcome: Parametric test of whether group means on a numeric outcome differ after statistically controlling for a numeric covariate.
ANCOVA.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether groups differ on average, after adjusting for another numeric variable's influence?
ANCOVA.dataType: Numeric outcome, one categorical factor, one numeric covariate
ANCOVA.mainAssumptions: Normally distributed residuals; homogeneity of variance across groups; homogeneity of regression slopes; linear covariate relationship
ANCOVA.resultMeaning: Adjusted group means and a test of whether they differ, after removing the covariate's linear effect.

andersonDarling.outcome: Tests normality (compatibility with a normal distribution), weighting deviations in the distribution's tails more heavily than the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
andersonDarling.typicalQuestion: Are these data plausibly normal? Which normality test is most sensitive to departures in the tails of the distribution?

ANOVAOneWayTwoWay.outcome: Parametric test of one or two categorical factors, including main effects and interactions.
ANOVAOneWayTwoWay.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether factors affect the numeric outcome, and whether they interact?
ANOVAOneWayTwoWay.mainAssumptions: Residual normality/constant variance; design balance helps
ANOVAOneWayTwoWay.resultMeaning: Main effects, interaction, F-tests and means.

ANOVAOneWayWithBlocks.outcome: Parametric test comparing treatment/group means while accounting for block-to-block variation.
ANOVAOneWayWithBlocks.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether groups differ after accounting for blocks?
ANOVAOneWayWithBlocks.resultMeaning: F-test, means, effects and residual variation.

ANOVAOneWayWithRanBlocks.outcome: Parametric test comparing treatment/group means while accounting for block-to-block variation.
ANOVAOneWayWithRanBlocks.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether groups differ after accounting for blocks?
ANOVAOneWayWithRanBlocks.resultMeaning: F-test, means, effects and residual variation.

ANOVANWay.outcome: Parametric test of three or more categorical factors, including main effects and interactions.
ANOVANWay.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether several factors affect the numeric outcome, and whether they interact?
ANOVANWay.mainAssumptions: Residual normality/constant variance; design balance helps
ANOVANWay.resultMeaning: Main effects, interactions, F-tests and means.

Anscombe.outcome: Test whether sample kurtosis differs from the normal-distribution expectation.
Anscombe.typicalQuestion: Is the distribution's tail/peakedness inconsistent with normality?

bartlettsTest.outcome: Test equality of variances across groups.

binomialTestSingleSample.outcome: Tests whether a single sample proportion differs from a hypothesized value using the exact binomial distribution (appropriate for small samples).
binomialTestSingleSample.typicalQuestion: Does the proportion of successes in my sample differ from a specific value, especially with a small sample?
binomialTestSingleSample.predictorType: N/A - single proportion vs. hypothesized value
binomialTestSingleSample.mainAssumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials; no large-sample approximation needed (exact test)
binomialTestSingleSample.resultMeaning: Exact p-value and confidence interval indicating whether the observed proportion differs from the hypothesized proportion.

Bonnett.outcome: Assess kurtosis using a robust/alternative kurtosis test.
Bonnett.typicalQuestion: Does the sample show non-normal kurtosis?

chiSquareAssociationSummarized.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; tests whether two categorical variables are associated, from a summarized contingency table of counts.
chiSquareAssociationSummarized.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test checks whether two categorical variables are associated with each other?
chiSquareAssociationSummarized.dataType: Categorical, entered as summarized counts (contingency table)
chiSquareAssociationSummarized.numberOfGroups: 2 categorical variables (rows x columns of table)
chiSquareAssociationSummarized.mainAssumptions: Independent observations; expected cell counts sufficiently large (typically ≥5) for the chi-square approximation to hold
chiSquareAssociationSummarized.resultMeaning: Chi-square statistic, p-value, and optionally residuals/contributions showing which cells drive the association.

chiSquaredTest.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; tests categorical independence or goodness-of-fit.
chiSquaredTest.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test checks categorical independence, or whether counts match expectations?

competingRisksOneGroup.outcome: Analyze time-to-event data when multiple mutually exclusive event types can occur.
competingRisksOneGroup.typicalQuestion: What is the incidence of different event types over time?

correlationTestMultivariable.outcome: Computes pairwise Pearson (parametric) or Spearman (non-parametric, rank-based) correlations (with significance tests) among two or more numeric variables.
correlationTestMultivariable.typicalQuestion: What is the relationship/correlation between two or more numeric variables? Which non-parametric test measures correlation without assuming normality?
correlationTestMultivariable.predictorType: N/A - symmetric pairwise relationship, no predictor/outcome distinction
correlationTestMultivariable.mainAssumptions: Pearson: bivariate normality and linear relationship. Spearman: monotonic relationship (rank-based, more robust to outliers/non-normality)
correlationTestMultivariable.resultMeaning: Correlation coefficient(s), p-value(s), and optionally a correlation matrix/heatmap showing strength and direction of relationships.

correlationTestMultivariableLegacy.outcome: Computes pairwise Pearson (parametric) or Spearman (non-parametric, rank-based) correlations (with significance tests) among two or more numeric variables.
correlationTestMultivariableLegacy.typicalQuestion: What is the relationship/correlation between two or more numeric variables? Which non-parametric test measures correlation without assuming normality?
correlationTestMultivariableLegacy.predictorType: N/A - symmetric pairwise relationship, no predictor/outcome distinction
correlationTestMultivariableLegacy.mainAssumptions: Pearson: bivariate normality and linear relationship. Spearman: monotonic relationship (rank-based, more robust to outliers/non-normality)
correlationTestMultivariableLegacy.resultMeaning: Correlation coefficient(s), p-value(s), and optionally a correlation matrix/heatmap showing strength and direction of relationships.

crossTabMultiWay.outcome: Assess association between categorical variables and compare observed/expected frequencies and proportions.
crossTabMultiWay.resultMeaning: Counts, percentages, expected counts, and association tests.

DatasetDatasetVariables.outcome: Produces summary statistics and histograms for one or more variables to explore their distribution.
DatasetDatasetVariables.typicalQuestion: What does the distribution of my variable(s) look like?
DatasetDatasetVariables.resultMeaning: Summary statistics (mean, SD, quantiles, etc.) and a histogram for each selected variable.

equalityOfVariances.outcome: Tests whether two or more groups have equal variances (homogeneity of variance).
equalityOfVariances.typicalQuestion: What tests can I run in BlueSky Statistics to test for homogeneity of variances?
equalityOfVariances.dataType: Numeric response, grouped by a categorical factor
equalityOfVariances.resultMeaning: Test statistic and p-value; a significant result indicates variances differ across groups (relevant before choosing e.g. pooled vs. Welch t-test/ANOVA).

factorAnalysis.outcome: Models a set of numeric variables as driven by a smaller number of unobserved (latent) factors.
factorAnalysis.typicalQuestion: Are my numeric variables driven by a smaller number of underlying, unmeasured constructs?
factorAnalysis.numberOfGroups: N/A (number of factors specified or auto-extracted)
factorAnalysis.mainAssumptions: Variables share common underlying variance (adequate correlation among variables); approximately linear relationships
factorAnalysis.resultMeaning: Factor loadings (which variables load on which factor), and optionally factor scores saved to the dataset.

frequencyTable.outcome: Produces frequency (count/percentage) tables for one or more variables.
frequencyTable.typicalQuestion: How are the values of my variable(s) distributed?
frequencyTable.resultMeaning: Counts and percentages for each observed value/level of the selected variable(s).

friedmanTest.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; compares 3+ paired/repeated conditions using ranks.
friedmanTest.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test compares repeated/paired conditions without assuming normality?

generateRuleBasketData.outcome: Runs association-rule mining (market basket analysis) to find "if X then Y" rules with support/confidence/lift, from basket-format transaction data.
generateRuleBasketData.typicalQuestion: What items tend to occur together, and how strong is that association?
generateRuleBasketData.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions for support/confidence estimates to be stable; frequent-itemset (Apriori-style) approach
generateRuleBasketData.resultMeaning: A set of association rules, each with support, confidence, and lift, ranked by strength of association.

generateRuleMultilineData.outcome: Runs association-rule mining (market basket analysis) to find "if X then Y" rules with support/confidence/lift, from long-format transaction data.
generateRuleMultilineData.typicalQuestion: What items tend to occur together, and how strong is that association?
generateRuleMultilineData.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions for support/confidence estimates to be stable; frequent-itemset (Apriori-style) approach
generateRuleMultilineData.resultMeaning: A set of association rules, each with support, confidence, and lift, ranked by strength of association.

generateRuleMultiVarFormat.outcome: Runs association-rule mining (market basket analysis) to find "if X then Y" rules with support/confidence/lift, from wide-format data (one column per item).
generateRuleMultiVarFormat.typicalQuestion: What items tend to occur together, and how strong is that association?
generateRuleMultiVarFormat.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions for support/confidence estimates to be stable; frequent-itemset (Apriori-style) approach
generateRuleMultiVarFormat.resultMeaning: A set of association rules, each with support, confidence, and lift, ranked by strength of association.

hierarchicalCluster.outcome: Groups observations into a hierarchy of nested clusters based on similarity across numeric variables.
hierarchicalCluster.typicalQuestion: Can I segment/group my observations based on similarity, without pre-specifying the number of groups?
hierarchicalCluster.numberOfGroups: Number of clusters chosen after inspecting the dendrogram (not pre-specified)
hierarchicalCluster.mainAssumptions: A meaningful distance metric (e.g. Euclidean); variables typically should be on comparable scales
hierarchicalCluster.resultMeaning: A dendrogram and cluster assignments showing how observations group together at different similarity levels.

ItemFreqPlotBasketData.outcome: Plots the frequency of items across transactions, from basket-format transaction data (one row per transaction, items in a delimited list).
ItemFreqPlotBasketData.typicalQuestion: Which items appear most often across my transactions?
ItemFreqPlotBasketData.resultMeaning: A bar chart of item frequencies (relative or absolute) across all transactions.

ItemFreqPlotMultilineData.outcome: Plots the frequency of items across transactions, from long-format transaction data (transaction id + item, one row per item).
ItemFreqPlotMultilineData.typicalQuestion: Which items appear most often across my transactions?
ItemFreqPlotMultilineData.mainAssumptions: Transaction id and item columns correctly identified
ItemFreqPlotMultilineData.resultMeaning: A bar chart of item frequencies (relative or absolute) across all transactions.

KaplanMeierEstimationCompareGroups.outcome: Estimate and compare survival curves across groups.
KaplanMeierEstimationCompareGroups.mainAssumptions: Non-informative censoring; proportional hazards not required for KM itself
KaplanMeierEstimationCompareGroups.resultMeaning: Survival curves, medians and group comparison.

KaplanMeierEstimationOneGroup.outcome: Estimate the survival function for one group.
KaplanMeierEstimationOneGroup.typicalQuestion: What is the probability of remaining event-free over time?
KaplanMeierEstimationOneGroup.resultMeaning: Survival curve, median/quantiles and event-free probabilities.

KMeansCluster.outcome: Partition observations into K relatively homogeneous clusters.
KMeansCluster.typicalQuestion: Can I segment observations into K groups?
KMeansCluster.mainAssumptions: Choice of K; scaling; Euclidean-like structure

kruskalWallisTest.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; compares 3+ independent groups using ranks.
kruskalWallisTest.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test compares 3+ independent groups when ANOVA assumptions are questionable?
kruskalWallisTest.mainAssumptions: Independent groups; similar distribution shape for location interpretation

kstest.outcome: Tests normality - whether a numeric variable's distribution differs significantly from a normal distribution - by comparing the sample's empirical distribution to a normal one.
kstest.typicalQuestion: Is my numeric variable normally distributed? Which normality test compares my data's distribution directly against a normal one?
kstest.mainAssumptions: Continuous data; parameters of the reference normal distribution are estimated from the sample, which reduces test power vs. a fully-specified reference
kstest.resultMeaning: Test statistic and p-value; a significant result suggests the variable is not normally distributed.

leveneTest.outcome: Test equality of variances robustly across groups.
leveneTest.mainAssumptions: Independent observations; robust to non-normality but still design dependent

MANOVA.outcome: Parametric test of whether group means differ across two or more numeric outcome variables simultaneously.
MANOVA.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether groups differ across several numeric outcomes considered together?
MANOVA.dataType: Numeric (2+ outcomes), one categorical fixed factor, optional numeric covariate(s)
MANOVA.mainAssumptions: Multivariate normality; homogeneity of covariance matrices across groups (Box's M); linear relationships among outcomes
MANOVA.resultMeaning: A multivariate test statistic (e.g. Pillai's trace, Wilks' lambda) indicating whether groups differ overall, plus optional post-hoc/estimated marginal means per outcome.

missingValueAnalysis.outcome: Summarizes the amount and pattern of missing data across selected variables.
missingValueAnalysis.typicalQuestion: How much missing data do I have, and where?
missingValueAnalysis.resultMeaning: Count/percentage of missing values per variable, optionally sorted or cumulative, to guide data-cleaning decisions.

multiDimensionalScaling.outcome: Represent similarity/dissimilarity relationships in a lower-dimensional map.
multiDimensionalScaling.typicalQuestion: How are observations/items positioned relative to each other?

oneSampleVariance.outcome: Tests whether the variance (or standard deviation) of a numeric sample differs from a hypothesized value.
oneSampleVariance.typicalQuestion: Does the variability of my measurements differ from a target/specification value?
oneSampleVariance.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal population (the chi-square test for variance is sensitive to non-normality)
oneSampleVariance.resultMeaning: Test statistic, p-value, and confidence interval for the variance/SD versus the hypothesized value.

pairedWilcoxon.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; tests paired changes using signed ranks.
pairedWilcoxon.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test checks whether paired observations changed, without assuming normality?
pairedWilcoxon.mainAssumptions: Symmetry of differences for strict interpretation

polychoricPolyserialCorrelations.outcome: Estimate association for ordinal-ordinal or ordinal-continuous variables under latent-continuous assumptions.

principalComponentAnalysis.outcome: Reduces a set of correlated numeric variables into a smaller set of uncorrelated components that capture most of the variance.
principalComponentAnalysis.typicalQuestion: Can I reduce many correlated numeric variables down to a few underlying dimensions?
principalComponentAnalysis.mainAssumptions: Linear relationships among variables; variables should be on comparable scales (or use the correlation matrix, not covariance)
principalComponentAnalysis.resultMeaning: Component loadings, variance explained per component, and optionally a scree plot / component scores added to the dataset.

proportionIndependentSamples.outcome: Tests whether the proportion of successes differs between two independent groups.
proportionIndependentSamples.typicalQuestion: Does the proportion of successes differ between two independent groups?
proportionIndependentSamples.dataType: Binary outcome grouped by a 2-level factor, or summarized counts
proportionIndependentSamples.mainAssumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials within/between groups; for normal approximation, adequate sample sizes
proportionIndependentSamples.resultMeaning: p-value and confidence interval for the difference in proportions between the two groups.

proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.outcome: Tests whether a single sample proportion differs from a hypothesized value, using exact or normal-approximation methods.
proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.typicalQuestion: Does the proportion of successes in my sample differ from a specific value?
proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.dataType: Binary (2-level categorical or 0/1), or summarized counts (events/trials)
proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.predictorType: N/A - single proportion vs. hypothesized value
proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.mainAssumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials; for the normal-approximation method, sample size large enough for the approximation to hold
proportionTestOneSampleBinomialMini.resultMeaning: p-value and confidence interval indicating whether the observed proportion differs from the hypothesized proportion.

proportionTestSingleSample.outcome: Tests whether a single sample proportion differs from a hypothesized value, using exact or normal-approximation methods.
proportionTestSingleSample.typicalQuestion: Does the proportion of successes in my sample differ from a specific value?
proportionTestSingleSample.dataType: Binary (2-level categorical or 0/1), or summarized counts (events/trials)
proportionTestSingleSample.predictorType: N/A - single proportion vs. hypothesized value
proportionTestSingleSample.mainAssumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials; for the normal-approximation method, sample size large enough for the approximation to hold
proportionTestSingleSample.resultMeaning: p-value and confidence interval indicating whether the observed proportion differs from the hypothesized proportion.

proportionTestTwoSampleBinomialMini.outcome: Tests whether the proportion of successes differs between two independent groups.
proportionTestTwoSampleBinomialMini.typicalQuestion: Does the proportion of successes differ between two independent groups?
proportionTestTwoSampleBinomialMini.dataType: Binary outcome grouped by a 2-level factor, or summarized counts
proportionTestTwoSampleBinomialMini.mainAssumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials within/between groups; for normal approximation, adequate sample sizes
proportionTestTwoSampleBinomialMini.resultMeaning: p-value and confidence interval for the difference in proportions between the two groups.

repeatedMeasuresAnovaL.outcome: Parametric test of changes across repeated conditions/time using long-format data.
repeatedMeasuresAnovaL.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether the same subject changes across time/conditions, using long-format data?

repeatedMeasuresAnovaW.outcome: Parametric test of changes across repeated conditions/time using wide-format data.
repeatedMeasuresAnovaW.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether the same subject changes across time/conditions, using wide-format data?

sampleMoment.outcome: Calculate sample moments describing distribution shape.
sampleMoment.typicalQuestion: What are the moments of my data?

shapiroWilkNormalityTest.outcome: Tests normality (compatibility with a normal distribution); generally the most powerful normality test for small-to-moderate sample sizes.
shapiroWilkNormalityTest.typicalQuestion: Are these data plausibly normal? Which normality test is generally recommended for small-to-moderate sample sizes?

shapiroWilkNormalityTestLegacy.outcome: Test compatibility with a normal distribution.

TableAdvanced.typicalQuestion: How can I present grouped results in a structured table?

TableBasic.typicalQuestion: How can I summarize variables by groups?

targetingItemsBasketData.outcome: Runs association-rule mining restricted to rules that lead to (or start from) a specific target item, from basket-format data.
targetingItemsBasketData.typicalQuestion: What items or combinations are most associated with a specific item of interest?
targetingItemsBasketData.predictorType: Items other than the target, as antecedents
targetingItemsBasketData.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions containing the target item for stable estimates
targetingItemsBasketData.resultMeaning: Association rules involving the specified target item, with support, confidence, and lift.

targetingItemsMultilineData.outcome: Runs association-rule mining restricted to rules that lead to (or start from) a specific target item, from long-format transaction data.
targetingItemsMultilineData.typicalQuestion: What items or combinations are most associated with a specific item of interest?
targetingItemsMultilineData.predictorType: Items other than the target, as antecedents
targetingItemsMultilineData.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions containing the target item for stable estimates
targetingItemsMultilineData.resultMeaning: Association rules involving the specified target item, with support, confidence, and lift.

targetingItemsMultiVarFormat.outcome: Runs association-rule mining restricted to rules that lead to (or start from) a specific target item, from wide-format data.
targetingItemsMultiVarFormat.typicalQuestion: What items or combinations are most associated with a specific item of interest?
targetingItemsMultiVarFormat.predictorType: Items other than the target, as antecedents
targetingItemsMultiVarFormat.mainAssumptions: Sufficient transactions containing the target item for stable estimates
targetingItemsMultiVarFormat.resultMeaning: Association rules involving the specified target item, with support, confidence, and lift.

ttestIndependentSamples.outcome: Parametric test comparing means of two independent groups.
ttestIndependentSamples.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether two independent groups have different means?
ttestIndependentSamples.mainAssumptions: Approximate normality; equal variance or Welch approach
ttestIndependentSamples.resultMeaning: Mean difference, CI, t-statistic and p-value.

ttestIndependentSamplesLegacy.outcome: Parametric test comparing means of two independent groups.
ttestIndependentSamplesLegacy.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether two independent groups have different means?
ttestIndependentSamplesLegacy.mainAssumptions: Approximate normality; equal variance or Welch approach
ttestIndependentSamplesLegacy.resultMeaning: Mean difference, CI, t-statistic and p-value.

tTestIndependentSamplesTwoNumericVars.outcome: Parametric test of the mean change between paired measurements.
tTestIndependentSamplesTwoNumericVars.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether the same subjects/items changed?
tTestIndependentSamplesTwoNumericVars.resultMeaning: Mean change, CI, t-statistic and p-value.

ttestOneSample.outcome: Parametric test comparing a sample mean with a target/reference value.
ttestOneSample.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether the population mean differs from a target?
ttestOneSample.mainAssumptions: Approximate normality or robust enough sample

ttestOneSampleLegacy.outcome: Parametric test comparing a sample mean with a target/reference value.
ttestOneSampleLegacy.typicalQuestion: Which parametric test checks whether the population mean differs from a target?
ttestOneSampleLegacy.mainAssumptions: Approximate normality or robust enough sample

UberSummary.outcome: Summarize numeric variables with descriptive summary statistics (min, max, mean, median, sum, standard deviation, quantiles), optionally grouped by a categorical variable.
UberSummary.typicalQuestion: How do I summarize my numeric variables? What are the central tendency, variability, and summary statistics (mean, median, min, max) of my data?

varianceTest2Samples.outcome: Tests whether two independent groups have equal variances, using the F-test.
varianceTest2Samples.typicalQuestion: What tests can I run to check for homogeneity of variance across two groups?
varianceTest2Samples.dataType: Numeric response, grouped by a 2-level factor
varianceTest2Samples.mainAssumptions: Both groups approximately normal (the F-test is sensitive to non-normality; Levene's test is a more robust alternative)
varianceTest2Samples.resultMeaning: F-statistic, p-value, and confidence interval for the ratio of variances between the two groups.

wilcoxonMannWhitney.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; compares two independent groups using ranks.
wilcoxonMannWhitney.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test compares two independent groups without a normality assumption?

wilcoxonOneSample.outcome: One of BlueSky's non-parametric tests; tests a location/median-type hypothesis using ranks.
wilcoxonOneSample.typicalQuestion: Which non-parametric test checks whether a sample differs from a target value?

partialCorrelation.outcome: Computes the semi-partial (part) correlation between pairs of variables, showing the correlation left after removing the effect of control variables from only one side of the pair.
partialCorrelation.typicalQuestion: What is the correlation between two variables after removing the effect of other variables from just one of them?
partialCorrelation.predictorType: Target variables (pairwise) plus one or more control variables
partialCorrelation.resultMeaning: Semi-partial correlation coefficient(s) and significance, showing the unique relationship between each variable pair net of the control variables.

semipartialCorrelation.outcome: Computes the partial correlation between pairs of variables, showing the correlation left after removing the linear effect of control variables from both sides of the pair.
semipartialCorrelation.typicalQuestion: What is the correlation between two variables after controlling for one or more other variables?
semipartialCorrelation.predictorType: Target variables (pairwise) plus one or more control variables
semipartialCorrelation.resultMeaning: Partial correlation coefficient(s) and significance, showing the relationship between each variable pair net of the control variables.

CumulativeStatisticVariable.outcome: Adds a new variable containing a running/cumulative statistic (sum, mean, min, max, etc.) of a numeric variable, optionally within groups.
CumulativeStatisticVariable.typicalQuestion: How should I prepare or restructure my data?
CumulativeStatisticVariable.mainAssumptions: Depends on data operation; typically requires the data to be in a meaningful row order (e.g. time-ordered) for cumulative statistics to be interpretable
CumulativeStatisticVariable.resultMeaning: A new column with the running cumulative statistic added to the dataset.

FactorLevelManualReorder.outcome: Reorders the levels of a categorical (factor) variable into a user-specified order.
FactorLevelManualReorder.typicalQuestion: How should I prepare or restructure my data?
FactorLevelManualReorder.resultMeaning: A modified/restructured variable (new or overwritten) with levels in the specified order, useful for controlling reference levels in later models/plots.

FindDuplicates.typicalQuestion: How should I prepare or restructure my data?
FindDuplicates.resultMeaning: Produces a modified/restructured dataset for downstream analysis.

SubsetByPosition.typicalQuestion: How should I prepare or restructure my data?
SubsetByPosition.resultMeaning: Produces a modified/restructured dataset for downstream analysis.

betaDistributionPlot.typicalQuestion: What does the Beta distribution look like for selected parameters?
betaDistributionPlot.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

betaProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Beta distribution at specified values.
betaProbabilities.typicalQuestion: What probability does the Beta distribution assign to this value/range?
betaProbabilities.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

betaQuantiles.outcome: Calculate quantiles/critical values from the Beta distribution.
betaQuantiles.typicalQuestion: What value corresponds to a specified percentile/probability under Beta?
betaQuantiles.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

binomialDistributionPlot.typicalQuestion: What does the Binomial distribution look like for selected parameters?
binomialDistributionPlot.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

binomialProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Binomial distribution at specified values.
binomialProbabilities.typicalQuestion: What probability does the Binomial distribution assign to this value/range?
binomialProbabilities.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

binomialQuantiles.outcome: Calculate quantiles/critical values from the Binomial distribution.
binomialQuantiles.typicalQuestion: What value corresponds to a specified percentile/probability under Binomial?
binomialQuantiles.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

binomialTailProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Binomial distribution at specified values.
binomialTailProbabilities.typicalQuestion: What probability does the Binomial distribution assign to this value/range?
binomialTailProbabilities.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

cauchyProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Cauchy distribution at specified values.
cauchyProbabilities.typicalQuestion: What probability does the Cauchy distribution assign to this value/range?
cauchyProbabilities.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

cauchyQuantiles.outcome: Calculate quantiles/critical values from the Cauchy distribution.
cauchyQuantiles.typicalQuestion: What value corresponds to a specified percentile/probability under Cauchy?
cauchyQuantiles.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

chisquaredProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Chi-Squared distribution at specified values.
chisquaredProbabilities.typicalQuestion: What probability does the Chi-Squared distribution assign to this value/range?
chisquaredProbabilities.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

chisquaredQuantiles.outcome: Calculate quantiles/critical values from the Chi-Squared distribution.
chisquaredQuantiles.typicalQuestion: What value corresponds to a specified percentile/probability under Chi-Squared?
chisquaredQuantiles.resultMeaning: Returns probabilities, quantiles, a plot, or simulated data for the specified distribution.

exponentialProbabilities.outcome: Calculate cumulative/tail probabilities for the Exponential distribution at specified values.

paretoChart.outcome: Plots categories ranked by frequency/count alongside a cumulative-percentage line, to highlight the "vital few" contributors.
paretoChart.typicalQuestion: Which few categories/causes account for most of my counts (the 80/20 rule)?
paretoChart.dataType: Categorical counts (long format: category + count, or wide format)
paretoChart.resultMeaning: A bar chart (descending frequency) with an overlaid cumulative-percentage line, highlighting which categories account for most of the total.

plotOfMeans.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales
plotOfMeans.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

qqPlots.outcome: Plots sample quantiles against theoretical distribution quantiles to visually assess whether a numeric variable follows a specified distribution (e.g. normal).
qqPlots.typicalQuestion: Does my numeric variable follow a normal (or other) distribution?
qqPlots.mainAssumptions: None required to draw the plot; used to visually check distributional assumptions for other tests
qqPlots.resultMeaning: A scatterplot of sample vs. theoretical quantiles; points following the reference line support the distributional assumption, systematic deviation refutes it.

stemAndLeaf.outcome: Show the distribution of numeric observations while retaining individual values.
stemAndLeaf.typicalQuestion: Show the distribution of numeric observations while retaining individual values.
stemAndLeaf.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales
stemAndLeaf.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

stripChart.outcome: Show individual observations and group distributions.
stripChart.typicalQuestion: Show individual observations and group distributions.
stripChart.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales
stripChart.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

threeAxisLineChartModal.dialog: Line Chart with two Y axis
threeAxisLineChartModal.outcome: Plots two numeric series against a common x-axis using two separate y-axis scales, to compare trends of different magnitude/units.
threeAxisLineChartModal.typicalQuestion: How do two numeric series trend together over the same x-axis, even if they're on different scales?
threeAxisLineChartModal.resultMeaning: A line chart showing both series' trends, each on its own y-axis scale.

twoDContourplot.outcome: Visualize density/response intensity over two dimensions.
twoDContourplot.typicalQuestion: Visualize density/response intensity over two dimensions.
twoDContourplot.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales

usCountyMap.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales
usCountyMap.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

usStateMap.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

violinPlot.outcome: Plots the distribution (density shape) of a numeric variable across levels of a categorical variable.
violinPlot.typicalQuestion: How does the distribution (not just the mean) of a numeric variable differ across groups?
violinPlot.resultMeaning: A violin (mirrored density) plot per group, showing distribution shape, spread, and modality side by side.

worldMap.mainAssumptions: Appropriate variable types and meaningful axes/scales
worldMap.resultMeaning: Provides a visual pattern; it is descriptive rather than a formal hypothesis test.

ppPlots.outcome: Plots sample cumulative probabilities against theoretical distribution probabilities to visually assess whether a numeric variable follows a specified distribution.
ppPlots.typicalQuestion: Does my numeric variable follow a normal (or other) distribution, judged by probabilities rather than quantiles?
ppPlots.mainAssumptions: None required to draw the plot; used to visually check distributional assumptions for other tests
ppPlots.resultMeaning: A scatterplot of sample vs. theoretical cumulative probabilities; points following the reference line support the distributional assumption, systematic deviation refutes it.

Contour.outcome: Visualize density/response intensity over two numeric dimensions using contour lines.
Contour.typicalQuestion: How does a response or density vary jointly across two numeric variables?
Contour.resultMeaning: A contour plot showing lines of equal density/response across the x-y plane.

Coxcomb.outcome: A polar-coordinate (rose-style) chart showing counts/values by category around a circle, with wedge area/radius encoding magnitude.
Coxcomb.typicalQuestion: How do counts or values compare across categories, shown as a polar/rose chart?
Coxcomb.dataType: Categorical grouping with a numeric or count value
Coxcomb.resultMeaning: A polar bar/rose chart where wedge size shows the magnitude for each category.

barChartModal.outcome: Plots a numeric variable's value (or count) as bar height across levels of a category, optionally split/colored by a second grouping variable, with optional mean-comparison error bars.
barChartModal.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable's total, count, or mean compare across categories, optionally by subgroup?
barChartModal.dataType: Categorical or any-type x variable, numeric y variable(s), optional categorical fill grouping
barChartModal.mainAssumptions: None (descriptive visualization); error bars/confidence intervals carry standard sampling assumptions when enabled
barChartModal.resultMeaning: A bar chart showing counts, sums, or group means (with optional error bars) across categories.

boxPlot.outcome: Plots the distribution (median, quartiles, outliers) of a numeric variable, optionally across levels of a categorical variable.
boxPlot.typicalQuestion: What is the distribution, spread, and outlier pattern of a numeric variable, optionally by group?
boxPlot.predictorType: Optional grouping (x-axis factor), optional fill factor
boxPlot.resultMeaning: A box-and-whisker plot per group showing median, IQR, and outliers.

density.outcome: Plots a smoothed estimate of a numeric variable's distribution (kernel density), optionally split/colored by a grouping variable.
density.typicalQuestion: What does the shape of my numeric variable's distribution look like, optionally by group?
density.dataType: Numeric (continuous), optionally with categorical color/fill grouping
density.resultMeaning: A smoothed density curve (or overlapping curves per group) showing the distribution shape.

frequencyFactor.outcome: Plots counts/frequency of a categorical variable's levels, optionally split/colored by a second grouping variable.
frequencyFactor.typicalQuestion: How many observations fall into each category, optionally broken down by group?
frequencyFactor.dataType: Categorical (any type, treated as discrete levels)
frequencyFactor.resultMeaning: A bar chart of counts per category, optionally stacked/grouped by a second factor.

heatMap.outcome: Visualizes a matrix of values as a colored grid, with row and column variables defining the grid and color encoding magnitude.
heatMap.typicalQuestion: How do values vary jointly across two categorical/grouping dimensions, shown as a color grid?
heatMap.dataType: Row and column grouping variables (numeric, categorical, or date)
heatMap.resultMeaning: A colored grid where cell color encodes the magnitude of the underlying value for that row/column combination.

histogram.outcome: Plots the frequency distribution of a numeric variable using binned bars, optionally split/colored by a grouping variable.
histogram.typicalQuestion: What is the shape (skew, modality, spread) of a numeric variable's distribution?
histogram.mainAssumptions: None (descriptive visualization); bin width affects the apparent shape
histogram.resultMeaning: A binned bar chart showing how observations are distributed across the range of the numeric variable.

lineChartModal.outcome: Plots a numeric y variable against an x variable (often time/sequence) as a connected line, optionally split/colored by group.
lineChartModal.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable trend over time or an ordered x-axis, optionally by group?
lineChartModal.dataType: Numeric y; x can be numeric, date, or ordered category
lineChartModal.mainAssumptions: None (descriptive visualization); assumes a meaningful ordering on the x-axis
lineChartModal.resultMeaning: A line chart showing the trend of y across x, one line per group if grouped.

pieChart.outcome: Plots the proportion each category contributes to a whole, as wedges of a circle.
pieChart.typicalQuestion: What share does each category contribute to the total?
pieChart.dataType: Categorical grouping with an optional numeric value (counts used if none given)
pieChart.resultMeaning: A pie chart with wedge size proportional to each category's share of the total.

scatterPlot.outcome: Plots two numeric variables against each other as points, optionally colored/sized/shaped by additional variables, with an optional smoothing line.
scatterPlot.typicalQuestion: How do two numeric variables relate to each other, optionally broken down by group?
scatterPlot.dataType: Numeric (continuous) x and y, optional categorical/numeric color/size/shape variables
scatterPlot.mainAssumptions: None required to draw the plot; a fitted smoothing line carries its own model assumptions if enabled
scatterPlot.resultMeaning: A scatter of points showing the joint relationship between x and y, with optional grouping and a smoothing/trend line.

scatterPlotMatrix.outcome: Plots pairwise scatterplots for 2+ numeric variables in a grid, to visually screen for relationships among many variables at once.
scatterPlotMatrix.typicalQuestion: How do several numeric variables relate to each other pairwise, all at a glance?
scatterPlotMatrix.predictorType: N/A - symmetric pairwise visualization, optional color grouping
scatterPlotMatrix.resultMeaning: A grid of pairwise scatterplots, letting patterns/relationships among multiple variables be scanned visually.

barChartPro.outcome: Plots a numeric variable's value (or count) as bar height across levels of a category, optionally split/colored by a second grouping variable, with configurable mean-comparison significance testing (t-test/Wilcoxon/Tukey HSD/Dunn/emmeans/Games-Howell) and p-value adjustment between groups.
barChartPro.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable's total, count, or mean compare across categories, optionally with a statistical test for whether group means differ?
barChartPro.dataType: Categorical or any-type x variable, numeric y variable(s), optional categorical fill grouping
barChartPro.mainAssumptions: None for the count/sum view; the selected mean-comparison test carries its own assumptions when significance testing is enabled
barChartPro.resultMeaning: A bar chart showing counts, sums, or group means with optional error bars and optional pairwise significance annotations between groups.

CompareROCCurves.outcome: Compare discriminatory performance of ROC curves/models.
CompareROCCurves.typicalQuestion: Is my model statistically adequate, interpretable, and useful for prediction?
CompareROCCurves.resultMeaning: Provides fit, uncertainty, comparison, diagnostic, or prediction evidence.

CoxSingleModel.outcome: Model how predictors affect the hazard/risk of an event over time.
CoxSingleModel.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
CoxSingleModel.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
CoxSingleModel.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

decisionTreesEZ.outcome: Predict/classify observations using recursive tree-based splits.
decisionTreesEZ.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
decisionTreesEZ.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
decisionTreesEZ.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

extremeGradientBoosting.outcome: Build boosted-tree predictive models for regression or classification.
extremeGradientBoosting.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
extremeGradientBoosting.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
extremeGradientBoosting.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

kNearestNeighbhors.outcome: Predicts/classifies a dependent variable by majority vote (or averaging) of the K most similar training observations.
kNearestNeighbhors.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict/classify a variable based on similarity to other observations - what analysis can you recommend?
kNearestNeighbhors.dataType: Any dependent variable type; numeric/categorical independent variables
kNearestNeighbhors.mainAssumptions: A meaningful distance metric between observations; variables typically should be on comparable scales; enough training data relative to K
kNearestNeighbhors.resultMeaning: A fitted KNN model, usable to score new observations (see "Make Predictions with KNN").

KNNPredict.outcome: Scores a new (or the same) dataset using an already-fitted K Nearest Neighbors model, producing predicted values.
KNNPredict.typicalQuestion: How do I apply my fitted KNN model to make predictions on new data?
KNNPredict.dataType: Requires the same independent variables used to train the KNN model
KNNPredict.predictorType: Independent variable(s) matching the trained model
KNNPredict.mainAssumptions: Prediction dataset's independent variables are on the same scale/coding as the training data
KNNPredict.resultMeaning: A new variable of predicted values added to the dataset.

linearRegression.outcome: Fits a linear model predicting a numeric dependent variable from one or more independent variables.
linearRegression.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict/explain a numeric variable - what analysis can you recommend?
linearRegression.dataType: Numeric dependent variable; numeric or categorical independent variables
linearRegression.mainAssumptions: Linearity, independent errors, homoscedasticity, approximately normal residuals, no severe multicollinearity
linearRegression.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates (effect of each predictor), R², and diagnostic plots (residuals vs. fitted, Q-Q, etc.) to assess fit.

linearRegressionLegacy.outcome: Fits a linear model predicting a numeric dependent variable from one or more independent variables.
linearRegressionLegacy.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict/explain a numeric variable - what analysis can you recommend?
linearRegressionLegacy.dataType: Numeric dependent variable; numeric or categorical independent variables
linearRegressionLegacy.mainAssumptions: Linearity, independent errors, homoscedasticity, approximately normal residuals, no severe multicollinearity
linearRegressionLegacy.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates (effect of each predictor), R², and diagnostic plots (residuals vs. fitted, Q-Q, etc.) to assess fit.

logisticRegression.outcome: Fits a model predicting a binary/categorical dependent variable from one or more independent variables, in terms of odds/probability.
logisticRegression.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict a categorical (e.g. binary) outcome - what analysis can you recommend?
logisticRegression.dataType: Binary/categorical dependent variable; numeric or categorical independent variables
logisticRegression.mainAssumptions: Independent observations, linearity between predictors and log-odds of the outcome, no severe multicollinearity
logisticRegression.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates (odds ratios), model fit statistics, and diagnostic plots for predicting the categorical outcome.

multiLayerPerceptron.outcome: Fits a feed-forward neural network to predict a dependent variable (numeric or categorical) from one or more independent variables.
multiLayerPerceptron.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict a variable using a flexible, nonlinear model - what analysis can you recommend?
multiLayerPerceptron.dataType: Numeric, ordinal, or nominal dependent variable; numeric, ordinal, or nominal independent variables
multiLayerPerceptron.mainAssumptions: No strict distributional assumptions, but requires enough data to train the network and careful tuning (learning rate, hidden-layer sizes, iterations) to avoid over/under-fitting
multiLayerPerceptron.resultMeaning: A fitted neural-network model usable for prediction/classification; typically evaluated on held-out data via modelEvaluation dialogs.

naiveBayes.outcome: Classify observations using a probabilistic Naive Bayes classifier.
naiveBayes.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
naiveBayes.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
naiveBayes.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

neuralNets.outcome: Fits a neural network to predict a numeric or categorical dependent variable from one or more independent variables, using the neuralnet R package.
neuralNets.typicalQuestion: I am looking to predict a variable using a flexible, nonlinear model - what analysis can you recommend?
neuralNets.dataType: Numeric or categorical dependent variable; numeric, ordinal, or nominal independent variables
neuralNets.mainAssumptions: No strict distributional assumptions, but requires enough data and careful tuning of network architecture to avoid over/under-fitting
neuralNets.resultMeaning: A fitted neural-network model usable for prediction; typically evaluated on held-out data.

optimalNoTrees.outcome: Determines the number of trees at which a tree-ensemble model's error stabilizes, to avoid over/under-fitting.
optimalNoTrees.typicalQuestion: How many trees should my boosted/ensemble model use?
optimalNoTrees.dataType: Depends on the fitted ensemble model
optimalNoTrees.predictorType: N/A - operates on an already-specified model configuration
optimalNoTrees.mainAssumptions: Same assumptions as the underlying tree-ensemble method
optimalNoTrees.resultMeaning: A plot of model error vs. number of trees, identifying the optimal (error-minimizing) number of trees to use.

partialCreditModel.outcome: Model ordered/partial-credit item responses using an IRT partial-credit model.
partialCreditModel.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
partialCreditModel.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
partialCreditModel.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

partialCreditMultiFacetedModel.outcome: Model ordered/partial-credit item responses using an IRT partial-credit model.
partialCreditMultiFacetedModel.typicalQuestion: Can I explain or predict an outcome with this model?
partialCreditMultiFacetedModel.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
partialCreditMultiFacetedModel.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

randomForest.outcome: Build an ensemble tree model for prediction/classification and assess variable importance.

randomForest.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event

ratingScaleModel.outcome: Model ordered rating-scale responses using an IRT rating-scale model.

ratingScaleModel.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event

simpleRaschMultiFacetedModel.outcome: Measure item difficulty and person ability/trait using a Rasch model.

simpleRaschMultiFacetedModel.dataType: Numeric, binary, ordinal, nominal, or time-to-event
simpleRaschMultiFacetedModel.resultMeaning: Estimated effects/predictions, uncertainty, fit measures, and/or classifications.

tuneRandomForest.outcome: Searches over the number of trees/predictors-per-split to find well-performing Random Forest hyperparameters for predicting a dependent variable.
tuneRandomForest.typicalQuestion: How do I choose good settings for a Random Forest model before fitting it?
tuneRandomForest.dataType: Any dependent variable type (numeric or categorical); mixed independent variables
tuneRandomForest.mainAssumptions: Same general assumptions as Random Forest (few distributional assumptions); tuning based on out-of-bag or cross-validated error
tuneRandomForest.resultMeaning: A plot/table of error vs. hyperparameter values (e.g. number of trees) to guide the final Random Forest configuration.

PrecisionAUC.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of the AUC
PrecisionAUC.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of a classifier/diagnostic test within a target precision.
PrecisionAUC.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to precisely estimate how well a classifier/diagnostic test discriminates?
PrecisionAUC.mainAssumptions: Assumed AUC value and class prevalence are realistic
PrecisionAUC.resultMeaning: Required sample size to estimate AUC within the specified precision.

PrecisionCorrelation.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of a Correlation
PrecisionCorrelation.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate a Pearson correlation coefficient within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionCorrelation.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to estimate a correlation precisely?
PrecisionCorrelation.mainAssumptions: Assumed correlation value is realistic; bivariate normality
PrecisionCorrelation.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around r.

PrecisionICC.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of the ICC
PrecisionICC.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate an Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (reliability) within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionICC.typicalQuestion: How many subjects/raters do I need to precisely estimate measurement reliability?
PrecisionICC.mainAssumptions: Assumed ICC value and number of raters are realistic
PrecisionICC.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the ICC.

PrecisionKappa.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of Cohen's Kappa
PrecisionKappa.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate Cohen's Kappa (inter-rater agreement) within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionKappa.typicalQuestion: How many subjects/ratings do I need to estimate inter-rater agreement precisely?
PrecisionKappa.mainAssumptions: Assumed Kappa value and category proportions are realistic
PrecisionKappa.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around Kappa.

PrecisionMeanDiff.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of a Mean Difference
PrecisionMeanDiff.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate the difference between two means within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionMeanDiff.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to estimate the difference between two group means precisely?
PrecisionMeanDiff.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal populations; assumed standard deviation is realistic
PrecisionMeanDiff.resultMeaning: Required sample size (per group) to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the mean difference.

PrecisionOneMean.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of a Mean
PrecisionOneMean.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate a single mean within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionOneMean.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to estimate a mean precisely?
PrecisionOneMean.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal population; assumed standard deviation is realistic
PrecisionOneMean.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the mean.

PrecisionOneProp.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of One Proportion
PrecisionOneProp.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate a single proportion within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionOneProp.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to estimate a proportion precisely?
PrecisionOneProp.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width.

PrecisionOR.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of an Odds Ratio
PrecisionOR.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate an odds ratio between two groups within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionOR.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to precisely estimate an odds ratio between two groups?
PrecisionOR.mainAssumptions: Assumed group proportions/odds ratio are realistic
PrecisionOR.resultMeaning: Required sample size to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the odds ratio.

PrecisionRiskDiff.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of a Risk Difference
PrecisionRiskDiff.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate the difference in risk (proportion) between two groups within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionRiskDiff.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to precisely estimate the difference in event risk between two groups?
PrecisionRiskDiff.resultMeaning: Required sample size (per group) to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the risk difference.

PrecisionRiskRatio.dialog: Sample Size, Precision of a Risk Ratio
PrecisionRiskRatio.outcome: Calculates the sample size needed to estimate the ratio of risks (proportions) between two groups within a target confidence-interval width.
PrecisionRiskRatio.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to precisely estimate the ratio of event risk between two groups?
PrecisionRiskRatio.resultMeaning: Required sample size (per group) to achieve the specified confidence-interval width around the risk ratio.

SampleSizeOneMean.dialog: Sample Size, Test One Mean or Paired Means
SampleSizeOneMean.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between one mean (or paired differences) and a reference value.
SampleSizeOneMean.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect a difference in one mean, or in paired before/after measurements?
SampleSizeOneMean.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal differences; specified effect size, standard deviation, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeOneMean.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned one-sample/paired t-test.

SampleSizeOneProp.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between an observed proportion and a null proportion.
SampleSizeOneProp.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect a difference in a single proportion?
SampleSizeOneProp.dataType: N/A - study-planning calculator, no dataset required
SampleSizeOneProp.mainAssumptions: Binomial sampling; specified effect size, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeOneProp.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned one-proportion test.

SampleSizeANOVANew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized effect size across 2+ group means (one-way ANOVA), with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeANOVANew.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need to detect a difference across several group means?
SampleSizeANOVANew.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal, equal-variance groups; specified effect size, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeANOVANew.resultMeaning: Required sample size per group (or achieved power) for the planned one-way ANOVA, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeCorrelationNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized correlation coefficient as different from a null value, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeCorrelationNew.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect that a correlation differs from zero (or another value)?
SampleSizeCorrelationNew.mainAssumptions: Bivariate normality; assumed correlation, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeCorrelationNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned correlation test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeOneMeanNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test One Mean or Paired Means New
SampleSizeOneMeanNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between one mean (or paired differences) and a reference value, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeOneMeanNew.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect a difference in one mean, or in paired before/after measurements?
SampleSizeOneMeanNew.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal differences; specified effect size, standard deviation, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeOneMeanNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned one-sample/paired t-test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeOnePropNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test One Proportion New
SampleSizeOnePropNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between an observed proportion and a null proportion, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeOnePropNew.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect a difference in a single proportion?
SampleSizeOnePropNew.dataType: N/A - study-planning calculator, no dataset required
SampleSizeOnePropNew.mainAssumptions: Binomial sampling; specified effect size, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeOnePropNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned one-proportion test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeSurvivalCoxNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test Cox Model New
SampleSizeSurvivalCoxNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized hazard ratio for a covariate in a Cox proportional-hazards model, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeSurvivalCoxNew.typicalQuestion: How many subjects/events do I need to detect a hazard ratio in a Cox regression?
SampleSizeSurvivalCoxNew.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; assumed hazard ratio, covariate standard deviation, event rate, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeSurvivalCoxNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size/number of events (or achieved power) for the planned Cox model test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroupNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Group Survival New
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroupNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized survival difference between two groups (e.g. log-rank test), with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroupNew.typicalQuestion: How many subjects/events do I need to detect a difference in survival between two groups?
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroupNew.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; assumed survival rates/hazard ratio, accrual/follow-up, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroupNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size/number of events (or achieved power) for the planned two-group survival comparison, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeTwoMeansNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Means New
SampleSizeTwoMeansNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between two independent means, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeTwoMeansNew.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need to detect a difference between two group means?
SampleSizeTwoMeansNew.mainAssumptions: Approximately normal populations; specified effect size, standard deviation, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeTwoMeansNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size per group (or achieved power) for the planned two-sample t-test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeTwoPairedPropNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Paired Proportions New
SampleSizeTwoPairedPropNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between two paired proportions (e.g. McNemar-type test), with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeTwoPairedPropNew.typicalQuestion: How many paired observations do I need to detect a difference between two related proportions (before/after, matched pairs)?
SampleSizeTwoPairedPropNew.mainAssumptions: Assumed discordant-pair proportion and difference in proportions are realistic
SampleSizeTwoPairedPropNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size (or achieved power) for the planned paired-proportions test, plus a power curve.

SampleSizeTwoPropNew.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Proportions New
SampleSizeTwoPropNew.outcome: Calculates the sample size (or power) needed to detect a hypothesized difference between two independent proportions, with an interactive power curve.
SampleSizeTwoPropNew.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need to detect a difference between two proportions?
SampleSizeTwoPropNew.mainAssumptions: Binomial sampling; assumed group proportions, alpha, and power are realistic
SampleSizeTwoPropNew.resultMeaning: Required sample size per group (or achieved power) for the planned two-proportion test, plus a power curve.

createCauseEffectDiagram.outcome: Identify and organize potential root causes of a quality problem.
createCauseEffectDiagram.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
createCauseEffectDiagram.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
createCauseEffectDiagram.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
createCauseEffectDiagram.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

cusumChart.outcome: Detect small persistent shifts in a process mean.
cusumChart.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
cusumChart.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
cusumChart.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
cusumChart.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

ewmaChart.outcome: Detect small/gradual shifts in a process using exponentially weighted observations.
ewmaChart.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
ewmaChart.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
ewmaChart.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
ewmaChart.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

GageBiasAnalysis.outcome: Determine whether a measurement system exhibits systematic bias.
GageBiasAnalysis.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
GageBiasAnalysis.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
GageBiasAnalysis.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
GageBiasAnalysis.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

gageRnR.dialog: Gage R&R - Measurement System Analysis, Basic
gageRnR.outcome: Quantifies how much of the variation in a measured variable is due to the measurement system itself (repeatability/reproducibility) versus true part-to-part variation.
gageRnR.typicalQuestion: Is my measurement system (gage/instrument/operator) reliable enough to trust the data it produces?
gageRnR.dataType: Numeric measured variable; categorical part and appraiser (operator/machine) variables
gageRnR.pairedIndependent: Repeated (each part measured by each appraiser, typically multiple times)
gageRnR.mainAssumptions: Parts and appraisers reasonably representative of production; multiple repeated measurements per part-appraiser combination
gageRnR.resultMeaning: Percent of total variation attributable to the measurement system (repeatability + reproducibility) vs. part-to-part variation, indicating whether the gage is acceptable.

mqccChart.outcome: Monitors process stability across multiple numeric quality-characteristic variables simultaneously using a multivariate control chart (e.g. Hotelling's T²).
mqccChart.typicalQuestion: Is my process stable when I need to monitor several correlated quality measurements together?
mqccChart.dataType: Numeric (2+ correlated quality characteristics), optional grouping variable for subgroups
mqccChart.mainAssumptions: Approximately multivariate-normal quality characteristics; a stable "Phase I" reference period to estimate control limits
mqccChart.resultMeaning: A control chart flagging out-of-control points/subgroups where the joint set of quality characteristics deviates from expected variation.

MultiVariChart.outcome: Visualize and diagnose major sources/patterns of process variation.
MultiVariChart.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
MultiVariChart.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
MultiVariChart.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
MultiVariChart.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

shewhartCharts2.outcome: Monitor process stability and detect special-cause variation using an appropriate control chart.
shewhartCharts2.typicalQuestion: What quality/process problem am I trying to diagnose, measure, control, or improve?
shewhartCharts2.predictorType: Process factors, operators, parts, time, specifications
shewhartCharts2.mainAssumptions: Depends on quality method and sampling design
shewhartCharts2.resultMeaning: Identifies causes, measures, capability, stability, agreement, or process variation.

SixSigmaOverview.dialog: Six Sigma reference tutorial by Thomas Pyzdek (Pyzdek Institute)
SixSigmaOverview.outcome: Displays an introductory/reference tutorial on Six Sigma methodology.
SixSigmaOverview.typicalQuestion: What is Six Sigma and what tools does BlueSky offer for it?
SixSigmaOverview.resultMeaning: Reference/tutorial content, not a statistical result.

lossFunctionAnalysis.outcome: Quantifies the economic "loss" from a process deviating from its target using a Taguchi-style loss function.
lossFunctionAnalysis.typicalQuestion: How costly is it when my process output drifts from its target value?
lossFunctionAnalysis.mainAssumptions: A meaningful target value and cost-at-tolerance-limit are known
lossFunctionAnalysis.resultMeaning: A plot and/or text summary of expected loss as a function of deviation from target.

processCapabilityQcc.dialog: Process Capability (does not handle missing values)
processCapabilityQcc.outcome: Assesses whether a process can reliably produce output within specification limits, computing capability indices (e.g. Cp, Cpk).
processCapabilityQcc.typicalQuestion: Is my process capable of meeting its specification limits?
processCapabilityQcc.mainAssumptions: Process is in statistical control; approximately normal output (or an appropriate transform)
processCapabilityQcc.resultMeaning: Capability indices (Cp/Cpk and related) and a capability plot indicating how well the process fits within spec limits.

shewhartCharts1.outcome: Monitor process stability over time using xbar and R/S control charts for a continuous, subgrouped measurement.
shewhartCharts1.typicalQuestion: Is my process in statistical control over time, based on subgroup means and variation?
shewhartCharts1.mainAssumptions: Rational subgrouping; approximately normal within-subgroup variation
shewhartCharts1.resultMeaning: Control charts (xbar plus R or S) with control limits, flagging out-of-control points/patterns.

shewhartCharts3.outcome: Monitor process stability over time using Individuals and Moving Range (I-MR) control charts for a continuous measurement with no natural subgrouping.
shewhartCharts3.typicalQuestion: Is my process in statistical control over time, when I only have one measurement per time point?
shewhartCharts3.dataType: Numeric (continuous), one observation per time point
shewhartCharts3.resultMeaning: Individuals and Moving Range control charts with control limits, flagging out-of-control points/patterns.

shewhartCharts4.outcome: Monitor process stability using Individuals/Moving Range charts that separate between-subgroup and within-subgroup variation.
shewhartCharts4.typicalQuestion: Is my process in control when variation comes from both between- and within-subgroup sources?
shewhartCharts4.mainAssumptions: Rational subgrouping; approximately normal variation at each level
shewhartCharts4.resultMeaning: Between/within control charts with control limits, flagging out-of-control points/patterns at each variation source.

idvar.typicalQuestion: How should I transform, encode, or clean a variable?
idvar.resultMeaning: Creates a variable in the form required for analysis.

lagorlead.outcome: Create lagged or lead values for sequential/longitudinal analysis.
lagorlead.typicalQuestion: How should I transform, encode, or clean a variable?
lagorlead.resultMeaning: Creates a variable in the form required for analysis.

attributeAgreement.outcome: Assesses whether appraisers consistently classify parts into the same categorical attribute, with themselves (repeatability), each other (reproducibility), and optionally against a known standard.
attributeAgreement.typicalQuestion: Do inspectors/appraisers agree with each other and with themselves when classifying parts into pass/fail or other categories?
attributeAgreement.dataType: Part/sample id, appraiser/operator id, categorical (nominal/ordinal) response, optional reference standard
attributeAgreement.pairedIndependent: Repeated measures (same parts rated multiple times)
attributeAgreement.mainAssumptions: Categories are mutually exclusive and consistently defined; parts are representative of the process range
attributeAgreement.resultMeaning: Agreement percentages/statistics for repeatability, reproducibility, and (if given) accuracy against a known standard.

loadDatasetFromPackage.dialog: Load a Dataset from a R Package
loadDatasetFromPackage.outcome: Loads a built-in sample dataset from an installed R package (e.g. datasets, MASS) into the data grid.
loadDatasetFromPackage.typicalQuestion: How do I load a sample/example dataset that ships with R, like mtcars or iris?
loadDatasetFromPackage.dataType: N/A - data loading utility, not an analysis
loadDatasetFromPackage.resultMeaning: The selected package dataset appears as a new dataset tab in the data grid.

TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.dialog: S/N (signal to noise) ratio and Taguchi (inner outer design) Summary
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.outcome: Computes the signal-to-noise ratio for a Taguchi inner/outer array design's response, summarized for a smaller-is-better or larger-is-better objective.
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.typicalQuestion: How do I summarize a Taguchi robust-design experiment's response using signal-to-noise ratio?
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.dataType: Numeric/scale response variable from a Taguchi design dataset
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.numberOfGroups: N/A - one response summarized across design runs
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.mainAssumptions: Data comes from a properly constructed Taguchi inner/outer array design
TaguchiParamAddSNSummaryPro.resultMeaning: S/N ratio summary table (and optional additional tables) for the chosen smaller-is-better/larger-is-better objective.

factorialSampleSizePro.dialog: Power and Sample Size for 2-Level Factorial (full or fractional) Design
factorialSampleSizePro.outcome: Calculates power or required replicates for a 2-level full or fractional factorial design, given the number of factors, effect size, and standard deviation, with an optional power curve/table.
factorialSampleSizePro.typicalQuestion: How many replicates do I need in a 2-level factorial DOE to detect a given effect size?
factorialSampleSizePro.dataType: N/A - design parameters (factor count, effect size, sigma, alpha), not dataset variables
factorialSampleSizePro.predictorType: N/A - design planning, not variable roles
factorialSampleSizePro.mainAssumptions: Effect size and standard deviation estimates are reasonable; model terms/blocks specified correctly
