factorialSampleSizePro.resultMeaning: Power (or required replicates) for detecting the specified effect, plus optional power-vs-effect and power-vs-replicates plots.

normalDistributionPlotPro.outcome: Plots the Normal density or distribution function for a specified mean/SD, with labeled/shaded regions between chosen bounds.
normalDistributionPlotPro.typicalQuestion: What does a Normal distribution with a given mean and standard deviation look like, with a shaded probability region between two values highlighted?
normalDistributionPlotPro.dataType: N/A - distribution parameters (mean, sd, bounds), not dataset variables
normalDistributionPlotPro.mainAssumptions: Data/process is assumed Normally distributed with the specified mean and SD
normalDistributionPlotPro.resultMeaning: A labeled Normal density/distribution plot, optionally with shaded probability region(s).

weibullDistributionPlotPro.outcome: Plots the Weibull density or distribution function for a specified shape/scale, with labeled/shaded regions between chosen bounds.
weibullDistributionPlotPro.typicalQuestion: What does a Weibull distribution with a given shape and scale look like, e.g. for modeling time-to-failure?
weibullDistributionPlotPro.dataType: N/A - distribution parameters (shape, scale, bounds), not dataset variables
weibullDistributionPlotPro.mainAssumptions: Data/process is assumed to follow a Weibull distribution with the specified shape and scale
weibullDistributionPlotPro.resultMeaning: A labeled Weibull density/distribution plot, optionally with shaded probability region(s).

reRun.outcome: Reproduces an existing output tab's analysis by swapping in different (but similarly structured) dataset(s) in place of the originals it used.
reRun.typicalQuestion: Can I re-run an analysis I already did, but on a new/updated dataset instead of redoing the whole dialog?
reRun.dataType: N/A - operates on an existing output tab and datasets, not raw variables
reRun.mainAssumptions: The replacement dataset(s) share the same variable names/structure the original analysis expects
reRun.resultMeaning: The original analysis re-executes using the newly mapped dataset(s), producing fresh output.

reRunOutputPro.outcome: Maps dataset(s) referenced in a previously saved/loaded output onto currently open dataset(s) so that output's analyses can be re-run.
reRunOutputPro.typicalQuestion: I loaded an old saved output - how do I point its analyses at the datasets I currently have open so I can re-run them?
reRunOutputPro.dataType: N/A - operates on dataset mappings, not raw variables
reRunOutputPro.mainAssumptions: The current dataset(s) have the same structure/variable names the old output's analyses expect
reRunOutputPro.resultMeaning: The old output's analyses re-run against the newly mapped current dataset(s).

cleanupExcelDataPro.dialog: Cleanup Excel or CSV data - adjust, delete rows and columns
cleanupExcelDataPro.outcome: Cleans up a messily-imported Excel/CSV dataset: removes specified/blank/constant rows or columns, promotes a row to column headers, and converts column data types.
cleanupExcelDataPro.typicalQuestion: My imported spreadsheet has junk header rows, blank columns, or wrong data types - how do I clean it up before analyzing it?
cleanupExcelDataPro.dataType: Any - operates on whole rows/columns regardless of type
cleanupExcelDataPro.predictorType: N/A - data cleaning, not variable roles
cleanupExcelDataPro.resultMeaning: A cleaned dataset (new or overwritten) with specified rows/columns removed, headers set, and column types converted.

importMinitabDatasetsPro.dialog: Import Minitab Dataset (file format supported - mwx and mpx)
importMinitabDatasetsPro.outcome: Imports a Minitab worksheet/project file (.mwx or .mpx) as a new BlueSky dataset.
importMinitabDatasetsPro.typicalQuestion: How do I bring a Minitab dataset (.mwx/.mpx file) into BlueSky Statistics?
importMinitabDatasetsPro.resultMeaning: The Minitab file's data appears as a new dataset in BlueSky.

splitRepeatColsPro.dialog: Split/Collapse a dataset with repeating group of variables
splitRepeatColsPro.outcome: Splits a dataset with a repeating block of variables (e.g. Day1_x, Day2_x, Day3_x...) into multiple datasets, or collapses such repeating columns into one long-format dataset.
splitRepeatColsPro.typicalQuestion: My dataset has repeating groups of columns (e.g. one set per time period) - how do I split them into separate datasets or collapse them into a long format?
splitRepeatColsPro.dataType: Any - operates on a detected or specified repeating column group
splitRepeatColsPro.predictorType: N/A - data reshaping, not variable roles
splitRepeatColsPro.mainAssumptions: The repeating variable-set length is either auto-detectable or correctly specified
splitRepeatColsPro.resultMeaning: One or more new datasets: either multiple split-out datasets, or one collapsed long-format dataset with a Set ID variable.

displayRules.outcome: Displays and sorts a previously generated set of association rules (from a rule-generation dialog), filtered/ranked by support, confidence, or lift.
displayRules.typicalQuestion: I already generated association rules - how do I view, sort, or filter the top N of them?
displayRules.dataType: N/A - operates on a saved rules object, not raw variables
displayRules.mainAssumptions: A rules object already exists from a prior association-rule-generation dialog
displayRules.resultMeaning: A table of the requested rules, sorted/filtered by the chosen metric.

missingValsColOutput.outcome: Summarizes missing values across the dataset's variables, one row per variable, showing counts/percentages missing.
missingValsColOutput.typicalQuestion: Which variables in my dataset have missing values, and how many/what percentage?
missingValsColOutput.resultMeaning: A table listing each variable with its count/percentage of missing values.

plotRules.outcome: Visualizes a previously generated set of association rules using a scatterplot, matrix, graph, or other rule-visualization layout, shaded by support/confidence/lift.
plotRules.typicalQuestion: I already generated association rules - how do I visualize them (as a scatterplot, network graph, matrix, etc.)?
plotRules.dataType: N/A - operates on a saved rules object, not raw variables
plotRules.mainAssumptions: A rules object already exists from a prior association-rule-generation dialog
plotRules.resultMeaning: A visualization of the rules using the selected plot method/engine, shaded by the chosen metric.

summaryStatsAllVarsControlLevels.outcome: Produces summary statistics for all dataset variables, capping the number of factor levels displayed per categorical variable (grouping remaining levels into "Other").
summaryStatsAllVarsControlLevels.typicalQuestion: How do I get quick summary statistics for every variable in my dataset, without a huge table of every factor level?
summaryStatsAllVarsControlLevels.resultMeaning: Summary statistics for every variable, with less-frequent factor levels collapsed into an "Other" category.

RSMFormula.dialog: Design of Experiments analysis with Response Surface Model (Quantitative)
RSMFormula.outcome: Fits a response surface model (quadratic regression) to a DOE dataset's numeric response, with optional contour/response-surface plots, steepest-ascent path, stepwise selection, and residual diagnostics.
RSMFormula.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a response surface model to my DOE data and see contour/response-surface plots?
RSMFormula.dataType: Numeric/scale response, optional force-kept numeric predictors, from a DOE design dataset
RSMFormula.mainAssumptions: Standard regression assumptions (normal, homoscedastic residuals); design supports quadratic-term estimation
RSMFormula.resultMeaning: Fitted RSM model with coefficients, diagnostics, and optional contour/response-surface/steepest-ascent plots.

exportDesign.dialog: Export Design - three files (csv, html, rda) will be created with the same name as the design
exportDesign.outcome: Exports the active DOE design to matching csv, html, and rda files on disk, for use outside BlueSky or to reload response data later.
exportDesign.typicalQuestion: How do I export my DOE design (with a place to add response data) to a file?
exportDesign.dataType: N/A - operates on the active design dataset as a whole
exportDesign.resultMeaning: Three files (csv, html, rda) written to the chosen path, matching the design's name.

importDesign.dialog: Import Design - must be a csv file with added response column(s) to the previously exported design
importDesign.outcome: Imports a previously exported DOE design csv file (with response column(s) added) back into BlueSky as a new dataset, ready for analysis.
importDesign.typicalQuestion: I exported my DOE design, ran the experiment, and added response data in a csv - how do I bring it back into BlueSky?
importDesign.mainAssumptions: The csv file matches the structure of a previously exported BlueSky design, with response columns added
importDesign.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing the design plus its response(s), ready for DOE analysis.

linearRegressionDoE.dialog: Design of Experiments (DoE) analysis - Advanced Linear Model (excluding center points)
linearRegressionDoE.outcome: Fits a linear model to a DOE dataset's numeric response (optionally excluding center/axial points), with residual diagnostics and observation-level statistics.
linearRegressionDoE.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a linear model to my DOE data, excluding center/axial points from the fit?
linearRegressionDoE.dataType: Numeric/scale response, optional weights variable, from a DOE design dataset
linearRegressionDoE.predictorType: Response (dependent), design factors (via formula), optional weights
linearRegressionDoE.mainAssumptions: Standard linear regression assumptions (normal, homoscedastic residuals)
linearRegressionDoE.resultMeaning: Fitted linear model with coefficients, diagnostics, and optional residual plots, based on the non-center/axial design points.

bootstrapResampling.dialog: Build a tuned model with Bootstrap Resampling
bootstrapResampling.outcome: Tunes a chosen model type's hyperparameters using bootstrap resampling, evaluating performance across resampled training sets.
bootstrapResampling.typicalQuestion: How do I tune a predictive model's hyperparameters using bootstrap resampling?
bootstrapResampling.dataType: Any (numeric/categorical) dependent variable, any-type independent variables
bootstrapResampling.mainAssumptions: Depends on the underlying model type selected
bootstrapResampling.resultMeaning: A tuned model object with resampled performance estimates across bootstrap iterations.

kFoldCrossValidation.dialog: Build a tuned model with k-Fold cross validation
kFoldCrossValidation.outcome: Tunes a chosen model type's hyperparameters using k-fold cross-validation, evaluating performance across folds.
kFoldCrossValidation.typicalQuestion: How do I tune a predictive model's hyperparameters using k-fold cross-validation?
kFoldCrossValidation.dataType: Any (numeric/categorical) dependent variable, any-type independent variables
kFoldCrossValidation.mainAssumptions: Depends on the underlying model type selected
kFoldCrossValidation.resultMeaning: A tuned model object with cross-validated performance estimates across the specified number of folds.

leaveOneOutCrossValidation.outcome: Tunes/evaluates a chosen model type using leave-one-out cross-validation (each observation held out in turn as the test case).
leaveOneOutCrossValidation.typicalQuestion: How do I evaluate a predictive model using leave-one-out cross-validation?
leaveOneOutCrossValidation.dataType: Any (numeric/categorical) dependent variable, any-type independent variables
leaveOneOutCrossValidation.mainAssumptions: Depends on the underlying model type selected; can be slow for large datasets since it fits N models
leaveOneOutCrossValidation.resultMeaning: A tuned model object with leave-one-out cross-validated performance estimates.

repkFoldCrossValidation.dialog: Build A Tuned Model With Repeated KFold Cross Validation
repkFoldCrossValidation.outcome: Tunes a chosen model type's hyperparameters using repeated k-fold cross-validation (the k-fold split repeated multiple times), evaluating performance across all repeats.
repkFoldCrossValidation.typicalQuestion: How do I tune a predictive model using repeated k-fold cross-validation for more stable performance estimates?
repkFoldCrossValidation.dataType: Any (numeric/categorical) dependent variable, any-type independent variables
repkFoldCrossValidation.mainAssumptions: Depends on the underlying model type selected
repkFoldCrossValidation.resultMeaning: A tuned model object with performance estimates averaged across repeated k-fold cross-validation.

computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.dialog: Compute model variable values to achieve target response
computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.outcome: Given a fitted model, computes the predictor variable value(s) needed to achieve a specified target value of the response.
computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.typicalQuestion: What input value do I need for my model to produce a specific target response?
computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model, not raw variables
computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit; assumes the fitted relationship holds in the target region
computeModelParamValuesTargetResponsePro.resultMeaning: The predictor value(s) that achieve the specified target response under the fitted model.

optimizeMultipleModelResponseDesirabilit.outcome: Finds predictor settings that jointly optimize multiple fitted models' responses using desirability functions, balancing competing objectives across responses.
optimizeMultipleModelResponseDesirabilit.typicalQuestion: I have multiple fitted models for different responses - what input settings jointly optimize all of them?
optimizeMultipleModelResponseDesirabilit.dataType: One or more numeric response variables, each from its own already-fitted model
optimizeMultipleModelResponseDesirabilit.mainAssumptions: Each response has an already-fitted model; desirability weights/targets reflect real priorities
optimizeMultipleModelResponseDesirabilit.resultMeaning: Predictor settings that maximize overall desirability across all specified model responses, with individual and composite desirability scores.

optimizeSingleModelMultipleResponseDesir.outcome: Finds predictor settings that jointly optimize multiple responses fit with the same model formula, using desirability functions.
optimizeSingleModelMultipleResponseDesir.typicalQuestion: I fit the same model formula to several response variables - what input settings jointly optimize all of them?
optimizeSingleModelMultipleResponseDesir.dataType: One or more numeric response variables, all sharing the same fitted model formula
optimizeSingleModelMultipleResponseDesir.mainAssumptions: Each response was fit with the same model formula/predictor structure; desirability weights/targets reflect real priorities
optimizeSingleModelMultipleResponseDesir.resultMeaning: Predictor settings that maximize overall desirability across all specified responses, with individual and composite desirability scores.

plotAModelPro.outcome: Produces diagnostic or effect plots for an already-fitted model.
plotAModelPro.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize/plot a model I already fit?
plotAModelPro.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
plotAModelPro.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit

summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.dialog: Summarize N Models with Residual Plots (e.g., models from Scatterplot model fit)
summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.outcome: Summarizes multiple already-fitted models side by side, including residual diagnostic plots for each.
summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.typicalQuestion: I fit several models (e.g. curve fits from Scatter Plot) - how do I compare their fit and residuals together?
summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.dataType: N/A - operates on multiple already-fitted models
summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.mainAssumptions: Multiple models have already been fit
summarizeNModelsScatterplotPro.resultMeaning: A side-by-side summary table/plots comparing the fitted models, with residual diagnostics for each.

binaryLogisticReliabilityPro.outcome: Fits a logistic regression relating a numeric input (e.g. stress, dose) to a binary pass/fail outcome, for predicting/reliability-style target-value estimation.
binaryLogisticReliabilityPro.typicalQuestion: How do I model the probability of pass/fail as a function of a numeric input, e.g. for a reliability or target-value study?
binaryLogisticReliabilityPro.dataType: Numeric input variable, binary (2-level) categorical response
binaryLogisticReliabilityPro.mainAssumptions: Binary response follows a logistic relationship with the numeric predictor; independent observations
binaryLogisticReliabilityPro.resultMeaning: A fitted logistic model predicting pass/fail probability from the input variable, usable for target-value/reliability estimation.

drcPro.outcome: Fits a dose-response curve model relating a dose/concentration variable to a response, optionally grouped and weighted.
drcPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a dose-response curve to my data?
drcPro.dataType: Numeric response and dose/concentration variables, optional grouping variable, optional weight
drcPro.mainAssumptions: The response follows a standard dose-response (e.g. sigmoidal) curve shape
drcPro.resultMeaning: A fitted dose-response curve with parameter estimates (e.g. slope, inflection point) and a fitted-curve plot.

mmrmPro.outcome: Fits a mixed-effect model for repeated measures (MMRM), modeling a continuous longitudinal outcome across visits/time within subjects, by treatment group.
mmrmPro.typicalQuestion: How do I analyze a longitudinal/repeated-measures continuous outcome (e.g. change from baseline) across visits and treatment groups?
mmrmPro.dataType: Continuous longitudinal outcome, treatment/group factor, visit/time factor, subject id, optional baseline covariates
mmrmPro.mainAssumptions: Outcome roughly Normal within groups/visits; correlation structure across visits within subject appropriately modeled
mmrmPro.resultMeaning: Fixed-effect estimates (e.g. treatment differences at each visit) accounting for within-subject correlation across visits.

nlsRegressionPro.outcome: Fits a nonlinear least-squares regression model relating a numeric response to a predictor, with optional weighting.
nlsRegressionPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a nonlinear regression curve to my data (not a straight line or polynomial)?
nlsRegressionPro.dataType: Numeric response and predictor variables, optional weight
nlsRegressionPro.mainAssumptions: The chosen nonlinear functional form is appropriate for the relationship; residuals approximately Normal
nlsRegressionPro.resultMeaning: A fitted nonlinear model with parameter estimates and a scatter/fitted-curve plot.

polyRegressionPro.outcome: Fits a polynomial regression model relating a numeric response to a numeric predictor (e.g. dose, concentration).
polyRegressionPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a curved (polynomial) relationship between two numeric variables instead of a straight line?
polyRegressionPro.mainAssumptions: A polynomial of the chosen degree adequately captures the relationship; residuals approximately Normal
polyRegressionPro.resultMeaning: A fitted polynomial regression model with coefficients and a fitted-curve plot.

responseScreeningPro.outcome: Screens multiple response variables against multiple predictor variables, quickly identifying which predictor/response pairs show the strongest relationships.
responseScreeningPro.typicalQuestion: I have many responses and many predictors - which pairs are most strongly related, before I build detailed models?
responseScreeningPro.dataType: One or more numeric response variables, one or more predictor variables
responseScreeningPro.mainAssumptions: Screening relationships are approximately linear/simple enough to rank via a quick fit per pair
responseScreeningPro.resultMeaning: A summary ranking predictor/response pairs by strength of relationship, to guide which to model in detail.

zeroInflatedRegressionPro.outcome: Fits a zero-inflated or hurdle regression model for count data with an excess of zeros, optionally with an offset and weights.
zeroInflatedRegressionPro.typicalQuestion: My count outcome has way more zeros than a normal Poisson/negative binomial model would predict - how do I model that?
zeroInflatedRegressionPro.dataType: Count (non-negative integer) dependent variable, optional offset, optional weights
zeroInflatedRegressionPro.mainAssumptions: Excess zeros arise from a separate process than the count-generating process (zero-inflation) or a genuine structural zero/positive-count split (hurdle)
zeroInflatedRegressionPro.resultMeaning: A fitted zero-inflated/hurdle model with separate coefficients for the zero and count components.

BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.dialog: Box-Cox transformation for a list of numbers (forward: original scale to transformed scale)
BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.outcome: Applies a previously stored Box-Cox lambda for a variable to transform a user-entered list of numbers from their original scale to the transformed scale.
BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.typicalQuestion: I already have a Box-Cox lambda for this variable - how do I transform a few specific numbers with it, without transforming the whole dataset?
BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.dataType: A variable with a previously stored Box-Cox lambda; numbers to transform entered manually
BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.mainAssumptions: A Box-Cox lambda has already been estimated/stored for the referenced variable
BoxCoxTransformNumbersPro.resultMeaning: The entered numbers converted to Box-Cox transformed scale using the stored lambda.

JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.dialog: Johnson transformation for a list of numbers (forward: original scale to transformed scale)
JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.outcome: Applies a previously stored Johnson transformation for a variable to transform a user-entered list of numbers from their original scale to the transformed (normalized) scale.
JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.typicalQuestion: I already have a Johnson transformation for this variable - how do I transform a few specific numbers with it?
JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.dataType: A variable with previously stored Johnson transformation parameters; numbers to transform entered manually
JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.mainAssumptions: A Johnson transformation has already been fit/stored for the referenced variable
JohnsonTransformNumbersPro.resultMeaning: The entered numbers converted to the Johnson-transformed scale using the stored parameters.

addRemoveJohnsonParamsPro.dialog: Add/Replace/Remove the Johnson transformation type and parameters for a variable
addRemoveJohnsonParamsPro.outcome: Manually sets, replaces, or removes the stored Johnson transformation type/parameters associated with a variable.
addRemoveJohnsonParamsPro.typicalQuestion: How do I manually set or clear the Johnson transformation parameters stored for a variable?
addRemoveJohnsonParamsPro.resultMeaning: The variable's stored Johnson transformation type/parameters are added, replaced, or removed.

addRepeatingPatternPro.dialog: Add a Variable of Repeating Pattern
addRepeatingPatternPro.outcome: Creates a new variable that cycles through a repeating pattern of values down the dataset's rows.
addRepeatingPatternPro.typicalQuestion: How do I add a variable that repeats a pattern of values (e.g. 1,2,3,1,2,3,...) down my dataset?
addRepeatingPatternPro.dataType: N/A - creates a new variable from a specified pattern, not derived from existing variables
addRepeatingPatternPro.resultMeaning: A new variable containing the specified repeating pattern.

inspectJohnsonParamsPro.dialog: Inspect Johnson transformation type and parameters for variables with prior Johnson transformation
inspectJohnsonParamsPro.outcome: Displays the Johnson transformation type and parameters currently stored for one or more variables.
inspectJohnsonParamsPro.typicalQuestion: What Johnson transformation type/parameters are currently stored for this variable?
inspectJohnsonParamsPro.dataType: One or more variables with a previously stored Johnson transformation
inspectJohnsonParamsPro.mainAssumptions: A Johnson transformation has already been fit/stored for the inspected variable(s)
inspectJohnsonParamsPro.resultMeaning: A table of each variable's stored Johnson transformation type and parameters.

inverseJohnsonTransformPro.dialog: Inverse Johnson transformation (convert back to non-transformed value)
inverseJohnsonTransformPro.outcome: Converts Johnson-transformed value(s) back to their original (non-transformed) scale, using a variable's stored or manually specified Johnson parameters.
inverseJohnsonTransformPro.typicalQuestion: I have a Johnson-transformed value - how do I convert it back to the original scale?
inverseJohnsonTransformPro.dataType: A variable with stored (or manually specified) Johnson transformation parameters
inverseJohnsonTransformPro.mainAssumptions: The Johnson parameters used match the ones originally applied to the value(s)
inverseJohnsonTransformPro.resultMeaning: The transformed value(s) converted back to their original, non-transformed scale.

johnsonTransformPro.dialog: Johnson transformation of non normal data to normal
johnsonTransformPro.outcome: Fits and applies a Johnson transformation to a non-normal variable, converting it to approximate normality.
johnsonTransformPro.typicalQuestion: My variable isn't normally distributed - how do I apply a Johnson transformation to normalize it?
johnsonTransformPro.mainAssumptions: The Johnson distribution family can adequately fit the variable's shape
johnsonTransformPro.resultMeaning: A new (or overwritten) variable transformed to approximate normality, plus the fitted Johnson type/parameters.

helpAbout.outcome: Displays version and general information about the BlueSky Statistics application.
helpAbout.typicalQuestion: What version of BlueSky Statistics am I running?

installRPackage.outcome: Installs one or more R packages by name from a CRAN repository into a selected library path.
installRPackage.typicalQuestion: How do I install an R package that BlueSky needs, or one I want to use in custom R code?
installRPackage.mainAssumptions: Network access to the specified CRAN repository; write access to the target library path
installRPackage.resultMeaning: The named R package(s) are installed to the selected library path.

rFunctionHelp.outcome: Looks up and displays R's built-in help documentation for a named function.
rFunctionHelp.typicalQuestion: How do I look up R help documentation for a specific function?
rFunctionHelp.resultMeaning: The requested function's R help page.

rInstalledPackages.outcome: Lists R packages currently installed, optionally filtered to a specific library path.
rInstalledPackages.typicalQuestion: What R packages are currently installed?
rInstalledPackages.resultMeaning: A list of installed R packages (and their library paths).

rPackageDetails.outcome: Displays version and other details for a selected installed R package.
rPackageDetails.typicalQuestion: What version of a specific R package is installed?
rPackageDetails.resultMeaning: Details (e.g. version) for the selected package.

rPackageHelp.outcome: Looks up and displays R's built-in help documentation for a selected installed package.
rPackageHelp.typicalQuestion: How do I view the help documentation for an installed R package?
rPackageHelp.resultMeaning: The selected package's R help documentation.

rSessionDetails.outcome: Displays details about the current R session (e.g. loaded packages, options, environment).
rSessionDetails.typicalQuestion: What does my current R session look like (loaded packages, settings)?
rSessionDetails.resultMeaning: Details of the current R session state.

rVersionDetails.outcome: Displays the version of R that BlueSky Statistics is running on.
rVersionDetails.typicalQuestion: What version of R is BlueSky Statistics using?

updateBlueSkyPackage.outcome: Updates the BlueSky R package itself, typically only run when directed by BlueSky technical support.
updateBlueSkyPackage.typicalQuestion: BlueSky support told me to update the BlueSky R package - how do I do that?
updateBlueSkyPackage.mainAssumptions: Should only be run when instructed by BlueSky technical support; requires write access and an app restart afterward
updateBlueSkyPackage.resultMeaning: The BlueSky R package is updated; the application must be restarted afterward.

CompareDatasets.outcome: Compares two datasets variable-by-variable and row-by-row, flagging numeric/text/factor differences beyond specified tolerances.
CompareDatasets.typicalQuestion: How do two versions of a dataset differ from each other?
CompareDatasets.mainAssumptions: The two datasets share a comparable structure (or a merge key is specified)
CompareDatasets.resultMeaning: A report of differences between the two datasets beyond the specified tolerance/matching rules.

CoxFirth.outcome: Fits a Cox proportional-hazards model with Firth's bias correction, useful for small samples or rare/quasi-complete-separation events.
CoxFirth.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a Cox survival model when I have a small sample or separation issues that make the standard Cox model unstable?
CoxFirth.dataType: Time-to-event (numeric), event indicator (0/1), predictors via formula
CoxFirth.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; Firth correction relaxes small-sample/separation instability
CoxFirth.resultMeaning: A fitted, bias-corrected Cox model with hazard ratio estimates.

LogisticFirth.outcome: Fits a logistic regression with Firth's bias correction, useful for small samples, rare events, or quasi-complete separation.
LogisticFirth.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a logistic regression when I have rare events or separation issues that make standard logistic regression unstable?
LogisticFirth.dataType: Binary/categorical dependent variable, predictors via formula, optional offset/weights
LogisticFirth.resultMeaning: A fitted, bias-corrected logistic model with odds-ratio-style estimates.

CoxWithFormula.outcome: Fits a Cox proportional-hazards model with a user-specified formula, optional weights, forest plot, and deviance-based tests.
CoxWithFormula.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a Cox survival model with a custom formula (interactions, transformations, etc.)?
CoxWithFormula.dataType: Time-to-event (numeric), event indicator (0/1), optional weights, predictors via formula
CoxWithFormula.predictorType: Time, event status, predictors, optional weights
CoxWithFormula.resultMeaning: A fitted Cox model with hazard ratios, optional forest plot and diagnostics.

SampleSizeANOVA.outcome: Calculates sample size, power, or detectable effect for a one-way ANOVA, given group means, standard deviation, and significance level.
SampleSizeANOVA.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need for a one-way ANOVA, given my expected group means and variability?
SampleSizeANOVA.dataType: N/A - design parameters (group means, sd, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeANOVA.mainAssumptions: Groups are independent, Normally distributed with equal variance (standard ANOVA assumptions)
SampleSizeANOVA.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power, or detectable effect - whichever was left unspecified) for the one-way ANOVA design.

SampleSizeCorrelation.outcome: Calculates sample size, power, or detectable correlation for testing a single correlation coefficient against zero.
SampleSizeCorrelation.typicalQuestion: How many observations do I need to detect a hypothesized correlation with a given power?
SampleSizeCorrelation.dataType: N/A - design parameters (correlation, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeCorrelation.mainAssumptions: Bivariate Normality of the two variables being correlated
SampleSizeCorrelation.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power, or detectable correlation) for testing the specified correlation.

SampleSizeSurvivalCox.outcome: Calculates sample size or power for testing a covariate's hazard ratio in a Cox proportional-hazards model.
SampleSizeSurvivalCox.typicalQuestion: How many subjects do I need to detect a given hazard ratio in a Cox regression?
SampleSizeSurvivalCox.dataType: N/A - design parameters (hazard ratio, event proportion, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeSurvivalCox.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; covariate distribution and event proportion estimates are reasonable
SampleSizeSurvivalCox.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power) for detecting the specified hazard ratio in a Cox model.

SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Group Survival
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.outcome: Calculates sample size or power for detecting a hazard ratio difference in survival between two groups (e.g. log-rank-type test).
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.typicalQuestion: How many subjects do I need to detect a given survival difference (hazard ratio) between two groups?
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.dataType: N/A - design parameters (hazard ratio, group allocation, event proportion, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards between groups; event proportion/allocation estimates are reasonable
SampleSizeSurvivalTwoGroup.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power) for detecting the specified between-group hazard ratio.

SampleSizeTwoMeans.outcome: Calculates sample size or power for a two-sample t-test comparing two independent group means.
SampleSizeTwoMeans.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need to detect a difference between two group means?
SampleSizeTwoMeans.dataType: N/A - design parameters (group means, sd, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeTwoMeans.mainAssumptions: Groups approximately Normal with the specified/similar variance
SampleSizeTwoMeans.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power, or detectable mean difference) for the two-group comparison.

SampleSizeTwoPairedProp.dialog: Sample Size, Test Two Paired Proportions
SampleSizeTwoPairedProp.outcome: Calculates sample size (number of pairs) or power for a McNemar-type test comparing two paired proportions.
SampleSizeTwoPairedProp.typicalQuestion: How many paired observations do I need to detect a difference between two related (before/after, matched-pair) proportions?
SampleSizeTwoPairedProp.dataType: N/A - design parameters (discordant-pair proportion, difference, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeTwoPairedProp.resultMeaning: Sample size (number of pairs, or power) for the paired-proportions test.

SampleSizeTwoProp.outcome: Calculates sample size or power for a two-sample test comparing two independent group proportions.
SampleSizeTwoProp.typicalQuestion: How many observations per group do I need to detect a difference between two group proportions?
SampleSizeTwoProp.dataType: N/A - design parameters (group proportions, power), not dataset variables
SampleSizeTwoProp.mainAssumptions: Sample sizes large enough for the proportion-test approximation to hold
SampleSizeTwoProp.resultMeaning: Sample size (or power, or detectable proportion difference) for the two-group proportion comparison.

AdvancedLineChartPro.outcome: Plots one or more numeric y variables against an x variable as connected lines, optionally split/colored by a grouping category, with more configuration than the basic Line Chart.
AdvancedLineChartPro.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable trend across x, optionally broken down by group, with more advanced line-chart formatting?
AdvancedLineChartPro.dataType: Numeric y variable(s), x variable, optional categorical grouping
AdvancedLineChartPro.resultMeaning: A line chart of y over x, optionally split/colored by group.

DendrogramPro.outcome: Plots a hierarchical-clustering dendrogram (tree diagram) for one or more numeric variables, optionally labeled by an id/batch variable.
DendrogramPro.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize hierarchical clustering of my observations as a dendrogram?
DendrogramPro.dataType: One or more numeric variables to cluster, optional label variable
DendrogramPro.mainAssumptions: A chosen distance/linkage method is appropriate for the data
DendrogramPro.resultMeaning: A tree diagram showing how observations merge into clusters at increasing distance.

Generate3DPlotPro.outcome: Plots three numeric variables against each other as points in a 3D scatterplot.
Generate3DPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How do three numeric variables relate to each other jointly, visualized in 3D?
Generate3DPlotPro.resultMeaning: A 3D scatterplot showing the joint relationship among the three variables.

HistogramPro.outcome: Plots the frequency distribution of one or more numeric variables as a histogram with an overlaid fitted Normal, Weibull, Log Normal, Exponential, or Gamma curve, optionally split/colored by a grouping variable.
HistogramPro.typicalQuestion: What does the distribution of a numeric variable look like compared to a fitted Normal, Weibull, Log Normal, Exponential, or Gamma curve, optionally by group?
HistogramPro.mainAssumptions: None to draw the histogram, depending on the overlay distribution selection, draw the appropriate overlaid distribution curve
HistogramPro.resultMeaning: A histogram with an overlaid Normal, Weibull, Log Normal, Exponential, or Gamma curve, showing how closely the variable's distribution matches Normal.

InteractionPlotPro.outcome: Plots mean response across levels of one or more categorical grouping variables, visualizing main effects and (with 2+ groupings) interactions between them.
InteractionPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How does the mean of my response change across factor levels, and do two factors interact?
InteractionPlotPro.dataType: Numeric response variable, one or more categorical grouping variables
InteractionPlotPro.mainAssumptions: None (descriptive visualization); interpreting interactions statistically requires an ANOVA-type model
InteractionPlotPro.resultMeaning: Line plots of mean response by factor level, revealing main effects and (if crossing) interaction patterns.

IntervalPlotPro.outcome: Plots a numeric variable's mean with an interval (e.g. confidence interval) across levels of one or more grouping variables.
IntervalPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How does the mean (with an interval/confidence band) of a numeric variable compare across categories?
IntervalPlotPro.dataType: Numeric y variable, one or more categorical grouping variables
IntervalPlotPro.mainAssumptions: Interval calculation (e.g. CI) assumes approximate Normality within each group
IntervalPlotPro.resultMeaning: A plot of group means with interval bars, letting group differences and precision be compared visually.

scatterPlotPro.outcome: Plots numeric y variable(s) against an x variable as points, optionally colored/sized/shaped by additional variables.
scatterPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How do two numeric variables relate to each other, optionally with point size/shape/color encoding additional variables?
scatterPlotPro.dataType: Numeric y variable(s), x variable, optional grouping/size/shape variables
scatterPlotPro.mainAssumptions: None required to draw the plot
scatterPlotPro.resultMeaning: A scatterplot of y vs x with optional color/size/shape encodings for additional variables.

TimeSeriesPlotPro.outcome: Plots one or more numeric variables over a date/time axis as connected lines, optionally split/colored by a grouping category.
TimeSeriesPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable trend over time, optionally broken down by group?
TimeSeriesPlotPro.dataType: Numeric y variable(s), optional date variable for the x-axis, optional categorical grouping
TimeSeriesPlotPro.resultMeaning: A time series line plot of the selected variable(s), optionally split/colored by group.

boxPlotMultiVariPro.outcome: Plots a numeric variable's distribution as box plots nested within multiple categorical grouping variables (a multi-vari chart layout).
boxPlotMultiVariPro.typicalQuestion: How does a numeric variable's distribution vary across a nested combination of several categorical factors?
boxPlotMultiVariPro.dataType: Numeric variable, x-axis categorical variable, optional additional nested grouping variable(s)
boxPlotMultiVariPro.resultMeaning: Box plots showing the numeric variable's distribution within each nested combination of grouping factors.

boxPlotPro.outcome: Plots the distribution (mean, median, quartiles, outliers) of one or more numeric variables, optionally across levels of a categorical variable and further split by a grouping variable.
boxPlotPro.typicalQuestion: What is the distribution, spread, and outlier pattern of a numeric variable, optionally by group?
boxPlotPro.dataType: Numeric variable(s), optional categorical x-axis variable, optional grouping variable
boxPlotPro.resultMeaning: A box-and-whisker plot per group showing mean, median, IQR, and outliers.

dotPlotPro.outcome: Plots individual observations of one or more numeric variables as dots along an axis, optionally split/colored by a grouping variable.
dotPlotPro.typicalQuestion: How are individual observations of a numeric variable distributed, optionally by group?
dotPlotPro.resultMeaning: A dot plot showing individual observation values, optionally split/colored by group.

paretoChartPro.outcome: Plots categories ranked by frequency/count (optionally using a specified counts variable) alongside a cumulative-percentage line, optionally as multiple side-by-side Pareto charts by group.
paretoChartPro.typicalQuestion: Which few categories/causes account for most of my counts (the 80/20 rule), optionally compared across groups?
paretoChartPro.dataType: Categorical variable, optional grouping variable, optional counts variable
paretoChartPro.resultMeaning: A Pareto chart (bars + cumulative line) highlighting the "vital few" contributing categories, optionally faceted by group.

QuantileRegression.outcome: Fits a quantile regression model, estimating the relationship between predictors and a specified quantile (e.g. median) of the dependent variable rather than its mean.
QuantileRegression.typicalQuestion: How do I model the median (or another quantile) of my outcome, instead of its mean, as a function of predictors?
QuantileRegression.dataType: Numeric/scale dependent variable, predictors via formula
QuantileRegression.mainAssumptions: Fewer distributional assumptions than OLS (robust to outliers/heteroscedasticity), but assumes the specified formula relationship
QuantileRegression.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates describing how predictors affect the chosen quantile of the outcome.

contrastsDisplay.outcome: Displays the currently set contrasts coding for one or more factor variables.
contrastsDisplay.typicalQuestion: What contrasts coding is currently set for my factor variable(s)?
contrastsDisplay.mainAssumptions: The variable(s) are genuine factors with contrasts already set
contrastsDisplay.resultMeaning: The current contrasts matrix/coding for the selected factor variable(s).

contrastsSet.outcome: Sets the contrasts coding (e.g. treatment, sum, Helmert) used for one or more factor variables in subsequent models.
contrastsSet.typicalQuestion: How do I change the reference level/coding scheme used for a factor variable in my models?
contrastsSet.resultMeaning: The selected factor variable(s) get the specified contrasts coding for future models.

glzm.outcome: Fits a generalized linear model (e.g. logistic, Poisson, Gamma) with a chosen family/link, dependent variable, and formula, with optional offset and weights.
glzm.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a generalized linear model (logistic, Poisson, etc.) with a custom formula?
glzm.dataType: Dependent variable (type depends on chosen family), predictors via formula, optional offset/weights
glzm.mainAssumptions: Depends on the chosen family/link (e.g. binomial for logistic, Poisson for counts)
glzm.resultMeaning: A fitted GLM with coefficient estimates on the chosen link scale.

linearRegressionFormula.outcome: Fits a linear regression model using a custom formula (interactions, transformations, polynomial terms, etc.), with optional weights.
linearRegressionFormula.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a linear regression with a custom formula, e.g. including interactions or transformed terms?
linearRegressionFormula.dataType: Numeric/scale dependent variable, predictors via formula, optional weights
linearRegressionFormula.mainAssumptions: Standard linear regression assumptions (linearity, Normal/homoscedastic residuals, independence)
linearRegressionFormula.resultMeaning: A fitted linear model with coefficient estimates for the specified formula.

loadAModel.outcome: Loads previously saved R model objects from a file back into the current session.
loadAModel.typicalQuestion: How do I load a model I saved earlier back into BlueSky?
loadAModel.mainAssumptions: None (file import utility); existing objects with the same name are overwritten
loadAModel.resultMeaning: The saved model object(s) become available in the current R session for evaluation/scoring.

logisticRegressionFormula.outcome: Fits a logistic regression model using a custom formula (interactions, transformations, etc.), with optional weights.
logisticRegressionFormula.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a logistic regression with a custom formula, e.g. including interactions?
logisticRegressionFormula.dataType: Binary/categorical dependent variable, predictors via formula, optional weights
logisticRegressionFormula.mainAssumptions: Binary outcome; log-odds linear in the specified predictors
logisticRegressionFormula.resultMeaning: A fitted logistic model with odds-ratio-style coefficient estimates for the specified formula.

mixedModelsBasic.outcome: Fits a linear mixed-effects model with a custom fixed-effect formula, a nesting/grouping unit for random effects, and optional random-slope variables.
mixedModelsBasic.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a mixed-effects model with random intercepts/slopes for a nesting unit (e.g. subject, site)?
mixedModelsBasic.dataType: Numeric/scale dependent variable, nesting/grouping variable, optional random-slope variables, fixed effects via formula
mixedModelsBasic.predictorType: Dependent, fixed effects, random effects (nesting unit, random slopes)
mixedModelsBasic.mainAssumptions: Random effects Normally distributed; residuals approximately Normal within groups
mixedModelsBasic.resultMeaning: Fixed-effect estimates plus variance components for the random effects.

multiNomialLogistic.outcome: Fits a multinomial logistic regression model for a categorical dependent variable with more than two levels, using a custom formula.
multiNomialLogistic.typicalQuestion: How do I model a categorical outcome with more than two levels as a function of predictors?
multiNomialLogistic.dataType: Categorical (3+ level) dependent variable, predictors via formula, optional weights
multiNomialLogistic.mainAssumptions: Independence of irrelevant alternatives; log-odds linear in the specified predictors (relative to a reference category)
multiNomialLogistic.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates for each non-reference category relative to the reference category.

ordinalRegression.outcome: Fits an ordinal regression model (e.g. proportional-odds) for an ordered categorical dependent variable, using a custom formula.
ordinalRegression.typicalQuestion: How do I model an ordered categorical outcome (e.g. low/medium/high) as a function of predictors?
ordinalRegression.dataType: Ordinal (ordered categorical) dependent variable, predictors via formula, optional weights
ordinalRegression.mainAssumptions: Proportional-odds assumption (effect of predictors is constant across the ordinal thresholds)
ordinalRegression.resultMeaning: Coefficient estimates describing how predictors shift the odds of being in a higher category.

saveAModel.outcome: Saves one or more fitted R model objects from the current session to a file for later reuse.
saveAModel.typicalQuestion: How do I save a model I fit so I can reload and use it later?
saveAModel.dataType: N/A - operates on already-fitted model objects
saveAModel.mainAssumptions: One or more models have already been fit in the current session
saveAModel.resultMeaning: The selected model object(s) are written to a file on disk.

sem.outcome: Fits a structural equation model (SEM), specifying latent variables, measurement model, and structural paths via a dedicated model-builder interface.
sem.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a structural equation model with latent variables and structural paths?
sem.dataType: Numeric/scale indicator variables, optional grouping variable for multi-group SEM
sem.predictorType: Latent variables, indicators, structural paths (all specified via the SEM model builder)
sem.mainAssumptions: Model is identified; indicators approximately Normal/continuous (or an appropriate estimator is chosen for categorical indicators)
sem.resultMeaning: Fitted SEM path coefficients, fit indices, and (if requested) measurement-model loadings.

GrubbsDetectOutlierPro.outcome: Tests one or more numeric variables for a single statistical outlier using Grubbs' test.
GrubbsDetectOutlierPro.typicalQuestion: How do I test whether my data has a statistical outlier?
GrubbsDetectOutlierPro.mainAssumptions: Data is approximately Normally distributed (aside from the potential outlier)
GrubbsDetectOutlierPro.resultMeaning: A test statistic and p-value indicating whether the most extreme value is a statistical outlier.

ROUTDetectOutlierPro.outcome: Detects outliers in one or more numeric variables using the ROUT method (robust regression and outlier removal), which does not assume Normality.
ROUTDetectOutlierPro.typicalQuestion: How do I detect outliers in my data without assuming it's Normally distributed?
ROUTDetectOutlierPro.mainAssumptions: Robust to non-Normality (that's the point of ROUT vs Grubbs)
ROUTDetectOutlierPro.resultMeaning: The observations flagged as outliers by the ROUT method.

ReshapeParametricSurvivalDataPro.outcome: Reshapes event/censor/total-units style survival data into the row-per-unit format needed for parametric survival analysis.
ReshapeParametricSurvivalDataPro.typicalQuestion: My survival data is in a summarized event/censor/total-units format - how do I reshape it for parametric survival analysis?
ReshapeParametricSurvivalDataPro.dataType: Event count, censor count, and/or total units columns
ReshapeParametricSurvivalDataPro.resultMeaning: A reshaped dataset with one row per unit, ready for parametric survival analysis.

WarrantyBuildNevadaFromTransactionalPro.dialog: Build Nevada Table from Shipment and Repair Warranty Data
WarrantyBuildNevadaFromTransactionalPro.outcome: Builds a Nevada-format table (shipment cohort by calendar/service month) from transactional shipment and repair warranty data.
WarrantyBuildNevadaFromTransactionalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I build a Nevada table from my raw warranty shipment and repair transaction data?
WarrantyBuildNevadaFromTransactionalPro.dataType: Transactional shipment and repair records (dates, quantities)
WarrantyBuildNevadaFromTransactionalPro.resultMeaning: A Nevada-format table of shipments and repairs by cohort and service period.

WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.dialog: Warranty Failure Probabilities in Nevada Table
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.outcome: Forecasts future warranty repair counts for a Nevada table, filling in future periods with predicted failure probabilities and optionally comparing forecast to actuals.
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.typicalQuestion: How do I forecast future warranty claims for cohorts still in the field, using my Nevada table?
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.dataType: Production/shipment month, units shipped, and (partially observed) monthly repair counts
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.predictorType: Cohort (production month), exposure (units shipped), observed/future repair counts
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.mainAssumptions: The failure-rate pattern from observed cohorts/periods extends to forecast future periods
WarrantyNevadaPredictionTablePro.resultMeaning: Forecasted repair counts/probabilities for future periods, optionally charted against actuals.

WarrantyParametricSurvivalIntervalPro.outcome: Fits a parametric survival model to interval-censored warranty failure-time data (known only to fall between a start and end time).
WarrantyParametricSurvivalIntervalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a parametric survival/reliability model when I only know failure occurred sometime between two inspection times?
WarrantyParametricSurvivalIntervalPro.dataType: Interval start and end time variables
WarrantyParametricSurvivalIntervalPro.mainAssumptions: The chosen parametric distribution (e.g. Weibull) fits the failure-time data
WarrantyParametricSurvivalIntervalPro.resultMeaning: A fitted parametric survival model with distribution parameter estimates from the interval-censored data.

WarrantyReshapeNevadaParametricSurvivalD.dialog: Reshape Nevada Warranty Data to Interval Censored Format
WarrantyReshapeNevadaParametricSurvivalD.outcome: Reshapes a Nevada-format warranty table (cohort x failure-count columns) into interval-censored row-per-unit format for parametric survival analysis.
WarrantyReshapeNevadaParametricSurvivalD.typicalQuestion: How do I convert my Nevada warranty table into the interval-censored format needed for parametric survival analysis?
WarrantyReshapeNevadaParametricSurvivalD.dataType: Cohort/shipment-month column, units-shipped column, chronological failure-count columns
WarrantyReshapeNevadaParametricSurvivalD.resultMeaning: A reshaped, interval-censored dataset ready for parametric survival analysis.

cmhPro.outcome: Tests association between two categorical variables while controlling for one or more stratification variables, using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test.
cmhPro.typicalQuestion: Are two categorical variables associated after controlling/stratifying for a third (confounding) variable?
cmhPro.dataType: Two categorical variables, one or more stratifying variables, optional pre-tabulated frequency counts
cmhPro.mainAssumptions: Consistent association direction/strength across strata (for the common-odds-ratio interpretation)
cmhPro.resultMeaning: A CMH test statistic/p-value and (typically) a common odds ratio across strata.

distributionFitPro.dialog: Fit of univariate distributions to non-censored data (with P-value)
distributionFitPro.outcome: Fits one or more candidate probability distributions to a numeric variable and reports goodness-of-fit p-values for each.
distributionFitPro.typicalQuestion: Which probability distribution best fits my data, with a goodness-of-fit p-value?
distributionFitPro.mainAssumptions: Observations are independent and identically distributed
distributionFitPro.resultMeaning: Fitted parameters and goodness-of-fit p-value for each candidate distribution, to help choose the best fit.

equivalenceTestPro.outcome: Tests whether the difference between one or two numeric variables' means falls within a pre-specified equivalence margin, rather than testing for any difference.
equivalenceTestPro.typicalQuestion: How do I show two things are practically equivalent (not just fail to find a significant difference)?
equivalenceTestPro.mainAssumptions: Approximately Normal data (or large enough sample); a meaningful equivalence margin is specified
equivalenceTestPro.resultMeaning: Whether the observed difference falls within the specified equivalence margin (i.e. practically equivalent).

frequencyTablePlotPro.outcome: Plots frequency counts for one or more categorical variables.
frequencyTablePlotPro.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize the frequency distribution of one or more categorical variables?
frequencyTablePlotPro.resultMeaning: A plot of counts/frequencies for each level of the selected variable(s).

parametricSurvivalDistFitPro.dialog: Parametric Survival Distribution Fit Analysis (Right Censored)
parametricSurvivalDistFitPro.outcome: Fits and compares candidate parametric survival distributions to right-censored time-to-event data.
parametricSurvivalDistFitPro.typicalQuestion: Which parametric distribution (Weibull, lognormal, etc.) best fits my right-censored survival/reliability data?
parametricSurvivalDistFitPro.resultMeaning: Fitted parameters and comparative goodness-of-fit for each candidate survival distribution.

parametricSurvivalIntervalDistFitPro.dialog: Parametric Survival Distribution Fit Analysis (Interval Censored)
parametricSurvivalIntervalDistFitPro.outcome: Fits and compares candidate parametric survival distributions to interval-censored time-to-event data.
parametricSurvivalIntervalDistFitPro.typicalQuestion: Which parametric distribution best fits my interval-censored survival/reliability data?
parametricSurvivalIntervalDistFitPro.dataType: Interval lower and upper bound time variables
parametricSurvivalIntervalDistFitPro.resultMeaning: Fitted parameters and comparative goodness-of-fit for each candidate survival distribution.

parametricSurvivalIntervalPro.outcome: Fits a parametric survival model to interval-censored time-to-event data.
parametricSurvivalIntervalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a parametric survival model when failure times are only known to fall within an interval?
parametricSurvivalIntervalPro.dataType: Interval lower and upper bound time variables
parametricSurvivalIntervalPro.mainAssumptions: The chosen parametric distribution fits the interval-censored failure-time data
parametricSurvivalIntervalPro.resultMeaning: A fitted parametric survival model with distribution parameter estimates.

parametricSurvivalPro.outcome: Fits a parametric survival model to (optionally right-censored) time-to-event data.
parametricSurvivalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a parametric survival/reliability model to my time-to-event data?
parametricSurvivalPro.mainAssumptions: The chosen parametric distribution fits the failure-time data; censoring (if any) is non-informative
parametricSurvivalPro.resultMeaning: A fitted parametric survival model with distribution parameter estimates.

parametricSurvivalSizeEstimatePro.outcome: Estimates sample size, test duration, or number of allowable failures for a parametric-survival reliability demonstration test plan.
parametricSurvivalSizeEstimatePro.typicalQuestion: How many units (or how long) do I need to test to demonstrate a reliability target?
parametricSurvivalSizeEstimatePro.dataType: N/A - design parameters (reliability target, distribution assumptions), not dataset variables
parametricSurvivalSizeEstimatePro.mainAssumptions: The assumed parametric survival distribution and its parameters are reasonable
parametricSurvivalSizeEstimatePro.resultMeaning: A test plan (sample size, duration, and/or allowable failures) meeting the specified reliability demonstration target.

aggregate.outcome: Aggregates one or more numeric variables by grouping factor/date variable(s), computing summary statistics (mean, median, sum, sd, etc.) per group, into a new dataset.
aggregate.typicalQuestion: How do I collapse my dataset to one row per group, with summary statistics for each group?
aggregate.dataType: Numeric variables to aggregate, factor/date grouping variable(s)
aggregate.resultMeaning: A new dataset with one row per group and summary statistics for each aggregated variable.

downSample.outcome: Randomly removes rows from the majority class/level(s) of a variable so all levels have the same (minority) count - useful for balancing class-imbalanced data.
downSample.typicalQuestion: My categorical outcome is imbalanced - how do I down-sample the majority class(es) to balance it?
downSample.mainAssumptions: None (resampling utility); reduces sample size, discarding majority-class observations
downSample.resultMeaning: A new, balanced dataset with equal counts across the specified variable's levels.

expandDataByWeights.outcome: Expands a dataset by repeating each row a number of times equal to its weight/count column, converting summarized/weighted data into one-row-per-observation format.
expandDataByWeights.typicalQuestion: My data has a count/weight column - how do I expand it into one row per observation?
expandDataByWeights.resultMeaning: A new dataset with each original row repeated according to its weight.

mergeDatasets.outcome: Merges (joins) two datasets together on common key variables.
mergeDatasets.typicalQuestion: How do I merge/join two datasets together?
mergeDatasets.dataType: Two datasets with a common key variable
mergeDatasets.mainAssumptions: The two datasets share a meaningful key/matching variable
mergeDatasets.resultMeaning: A new merged dataset combining columns/rows from both datasets by the matching key.

mergeDatasetsNew.outcome: Merges (joins) two or more datasets together on common key variables.
mergeDatasetsNew.typicalQuestion: How do I merge/join two or more datasets together?
mergeDatasetsNew.dataType: Two or more datasets with a common key variable
mergeDatasetsNew.mainAssumptions: The datasets share a meaningful key/matching variable
mergeDatasetsNew.resultMeaning: A new merged dataset combining columns/rows from the input datasets by the matching key.

randomSplit.outcome: Randomly splits a dataset into two or more subsets (e.g. training/test), adding a split-indicator variable or creating separate datasets.
randomSplit.typicalQuestion: How do I randomly split my dataset into training and test sets?
randomSplit.mainAssumptions: Rows are exchangeable (a simple random split is appropriate, no stratification needed)
randomSplit.resultMeaning: The dataset split into the specified random subsets/proportions.

removeSplit.outcome: Removes a previously set split/grouping definition from the dataset.
removeSplit.typicalQuestion: How do I remove a split I previously set on my dataset?
removeSplit.mainAssumptions: A split has previously been set on the dataset
removeSplit.resultMeaning: The dataset's split definition is removed.

reorderDatasetVariables.outcome: Reorders all variables in the dataset alphabetically by name.
reorderDatasetVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I reorder my dataset's columns alphabetically?
reorderDatasetVariables.dataType: N/A - operates on the whole dataset's column order
reorderDatasetVariables.resultMeaning: The dataset's columns are reordered alphabetically.

reshapeLongToWide.outcome: Reshapes a long-format dataset into wide format, spreading a repeated factor variable's levels into separate columns holding the repeated value variable(s).
reshapeLongToWide.typicalQuestion: How do I convert my long-format data (one row per observation-time) into wide format (one row per subject, one column per time)?
reshapeLongToWide.dataType: A repeated factor variable and repeated value variable(s), plus identifying variables
reshapeLongToWide.mainAssumptions: Each combination of identifying variables and factor level has at most one value (no duplicates)
reshapeLongToWide.resultMeaning: A new wide-format dataset with one row per identifying combination and one column per factor level.

reshapeWideToLong.outcome: Reshapes a wide-format dataset into long format, stacking multiple columns into a single repeated-measure variable and value column.
reshapeWideToLong.typicalQuestion: How do I convert my wide-format data (one column per time point) into long format (one row per subject-time)?
reshapeWideToLong.dataType: Multiple columns representing the same measure across repeated conditions/time
reshapeWideToLong.mainAssumptions: The selected columns genuinely represent repeated measures of the same underlying variable
reshapeWideToLong.resultMeaning: A new long-format dataset with one row per original-row/repeated-column combination.

sample.outcome: Draws a random sample of rows from the dataset (with or without replacement).
sample.typicalQuestion: How do I take a random sample of rows from my dataset?
sample.mainAssumptions: Rows are exchangeable (a simple random sample is appropriate)
sample.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing the randomly sampled rows.

setSplit.outcome: Sets a grouping (split) definition on the dataset by one or more variables, so subsequent analyses can be run separately per group.
setSplit.typicalQuestion: How do I split my dataset by a grouping variable so analyses run separately per group?
setSplit.dataType: One or more categorical (or other) variables to split by
setSplit.resultMeaning: The dataset gets a split definition; subsequent analyses run per group.

sortDataset.outcome: Sorts the dataset's rows by one or more variables.
sortDataset.typicalQuestion: How do I sort my dataset by one or more columns?
sortDataset.dataType: Any (one or more variables to sort by)
sortDataset.resultMeaning: The dataset's rows reordered by the specified sort variable(s).

sortDatasetsNew.outcome: Sorts the dataset's rows by one or more variables, ascending or descending.
sortDatasetsNew.typicalQuestion: How do I sort my dataset by one or more columns?
sortDatasetsNew.dataType: Any (one or more variables to sort by)
sortDatasetsNew.resultMeaning: The dataset's rows reordered by the specified sort variable(s).

stackDatasets.outcome: Stacks two or more datasets on top of each other (row-binds), optionally tracking which original dataset each row came from.
stackDatasets.typicalQuestion: How do I combine two or more datasets by stacking their rows together?
stackDatasets.dataType: Two or more datasets sharing similar variables
stackDatasets.mainAssumptions: The datasets share comparable variable names/structure for the stack to make sense
stackDatasets.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing the stacked rows of all input datasets.

stratifiedSample.outcome: Splits the dataset into subsets while preserving the proportions of a specified stratifying variable's levels in each subset.
stratifiedSample.typicalQuestion: How do I split my dataset (e.g. into train/test) while keeping the same proportion of each category in each split?
stratifiedSample.dataType: A categorical variable to stratify by
stratifiedSample.mainAssumptions: None (preserves the stratifying variable's distribution across splits)
stratifiedSample.resultMeaning: The dataset split into subsets with proportional representation of the stratifying variable.

subsetDataset.outcome: Creates a new dataset containing only the selected variables (and optionally rows) from the original.
subsetDataset.typicalQuestion: How do I create a smaller dataset with just the variables I need?
subsetDataset.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing only the selected variables/rows.

subsetOutput.outcome: Creates a new dataset containing only the selected variables from the original.
subsetOutput.typicalQuestion: How do I create a smaller dataset with just the variables I need?
subsetOutput.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing only the selected variables.

transposeEntireDataset.outcome: Transposes the entire dataset, swapping rows and columns.
transposeEntireDataset.typicalQuestion: How do I transpose my whole dataset (rows become columns)?
transposeEntireDataset.resultMeaning: A new dataset with rows and columns swapped.

transposeSelectVariables.outcome: Transposes only the selected variables of a dataset, swapping their rows and columns.
transposeSelectVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I transpose just a few specific columns of my dataset?
transposeSelectVariables.resultMeaning: A new dataset with the selected variables transposed.

upSample.outcome: Randomly duplicates rows from the minority class/level(s) of a variable so all levels have the same (majority) count - useful for balancing class-imbalanced data.
upSample.typicalQuestion: My categorical outcome is imbalanced - how do I up-sample the minority class(es) to balance it?
upSample.mainAssumptions: None (resampling utility); increases sample size by duplicating minority-class observations
upSample.resultMeaning: A new, balanced dataset with equal counts across the specified variable's levels.

AttributeAgreementPro.outcome: Assesses whether appraisers consistently classify parts into the same categorical attribute, with themselves, each other, and optionally against a known standard, with optional replicate trials.
AttributeAgreementPro.typicalQuestion: Do inspectors agree with each other and themselves when classifying parts, including across repeated trials?
AttributeAgreementPro.dataType: Part/sample id, appraiser/operator id, categorical response, optional reference standard, optional trial number
AttributeAgreementPro.mainAssumptions: Categories are mutually exclusive and consistently defined; parts representative of the process range
AttributeAgreementPro.resultMeaning: Agreement statistics for repeatability, reproducibility, and (if given) accuracy against a standard, across trials.

GageBiasAnalysisPro.outcome: Assesses measurement system bias by comparing measured values against known reference/standard values for a set of parts.
GageBiasAnalysisPro.typicalQuestion: Is my measurement system biased relative to known reference/standard values?
GageBiasAnalysisPro.dataType: Part id, measured value, reference/standard value, optional bias variable
GageBiasAnalysisPro.resultMeaning: Bias estimate(s) and significance test for whether the measurement system systematically over/under-measures.

addMovingAvgPro.dialog: Compute and Add a Moving Average Variable
addMovingAvgPro.outcome: Creates a new variable containing the moving average of a numeric variable over a specified window.
addMovingAvgPro.typicalQuestion: How do I add a moving-average smoothed version of a variable to my dataset?
addMovingAvgPro.mainAssumptions: Data is ordered meaningfully (e.g. by time) for the moving average to be meaningful
addMovingAvgPro.resultMeaning: A new variable containing the moving average of the selected variable.

addRecalibratedSampleGroupPro.dialog: Add a Recalibrated Sample Number Variable
addRecalibratedSampleGroupPro.outcome: Creates a recalibrated sample/subgroup number variable, adjusting an existing sample numbering scheme.
addRecalibratedSampleGroupPro.typicalQuestion: How do I recalibrate/renumber my sample or subgroup identifiers?
addRecalibratedSampleGroupPro.resultMeaning: A new variable containing the recalibrated sample numbers.

addSampleGroupPro.outcome: Creates a sample/subgroup number variable, grouping rows into sequential subgroups of a specified size.
addSampleGroupPro.typicalQuestion: How do I add a subgroup/sample number variable for control-chart subgrouping?
addSampleGroupPro.dataType: N/A - creates a new variable from row sequence
addSampleGroupPro.mainAssumptions: Rows are in the intended process/time order
addSampleGroupPro.resultMeaning: A new variable assigning each row to a sequential sample/subgroup number.

automotiveGageRRPro.outcome: Performs a Gage R&R (repeatability and reproducibility) measurement system analysis using the automotive industry (AIAG) methodology.
automotiveGageRRPro.typicalQuestion: How much of my measurement variation is due to the gage vs the appraisers vs the parts, using the AIAG/automotive method?
automotiveGageRRPro.dataType: Numeric measurement, part id, appraiser/operator id, optional reference values
automotiveGageRRPro.pairedIndependent: Repeated measures (each appraiser measures each part multiple times)
automotiveGageRRPro.mainAssumptions: Parts and appraisers are representative of the process; measurements are repeated per part/appraiser combination
automotiveGageRRPro.resultMeaning: Variance components (repeatability, reproducibility, part-to-part) and %GRR to judge measurement system adequacy.

binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.dialog: Binomial one-sided lower confidence bound for reliability
binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.outcome: Computes a one-sided lower confidence bound for reliability (proportion passing) based on a binomial pass/fail test result.
binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.typicalQuestion: Given a certain number of passes/failures in a reliability test, what is the lower confidence bound on the true reliability?
binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.dataType: N/A - test result parameters (successes, trials, confidence level), not dataset variables
binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.mainAssumptions: Test units are independent with a constant true reliability (binomial model)
binomialOneSidedReliabilityPro.resultMeaning: A one-sided lower confidence bound on the true reliability/pass proportion.

consistencyChartMSAPro.outcome: Plots repeated measurement system readings over time/index to visualize consistency and detect drift or instability.
consistencyChartMSAPro.typicalQuestion: Is my measurement system's output consistent over time, or is it drifting?
consistencyChartMSAPro.mainAssumptions: Measurements are taken under stable conditions aside from the time trend being investigated
consistencyChartMSAPro.resultMeaning: A chart of measurements over time/index, revealing drift or instability in the measurement system.

createMSAStudyDoEgridPro.dialog: Create an Experiment Table for a MSA Gage Study
createMSAStudyDoEgridPro.outcome: Generates an experiment/data-collection table (parts x appraisers x trials grid) for planning a Gage R&R or other MSA study.
createMSAStudyDoEgridPro.typicalQuestion: How do I set up the data-collection grid for a Gage R&R study before I go collect measurements?
createMSAStudyDoEgridPro.dataType: N/A - design parameters (number of parts, appraisers, trials), not dataset variables
createMSAStudyDoEgridPro.resultMeaning: A new dataset/table laid out for recording the planned MSA study's measurements.

gageRnRPro.outcome: Performs a Gage R&R (repeatability and reproducibility) measurement system analysis, decomposing measurement variation into gage, appraiser, and part-to-part components.
gageRnRPro.typicalQuestion: How much of my measurement variation is due to the gage vs the appraisers vs the parts?
gageRnRPro.dataType: Numeric measurement, part variable, appraiser variable
gageRnRPro.pairedIndependent: Repeated measures (each appraiser measures each part multiple times)
gageRnRPro.mainAssumptions: Parts and appraisers are representative of the process; measurements repeated per part/appraiser combination
gageRnRPro.resultMeaning: Variance components (repeatability, reproducibility, part-to-part) and %GRR to judge measurement system adequacy.

johnsonCapabilityPro.dialog: Process Capability Analysis (non-normal data with Johnson Transformation)
johnsonCapabilityPro.outcome: Performs process capability analysis on non-normal data by first applying a Johnson transformation to normalize it.
johnsonCapabilityPro.typicalQuestion: How do I assess process capability when my data isn't Normally distributed?
johnsonCapabilityPro.dataType: Numeric variable (observed process data, original non-normal scale)
johnsonCapabilityPro.mainAssumptions: The Johnson distribution family can adequately normalize the data's shape
johnsonCapabilityPro.resultMeaning: Process capability indices (e.g. Cp/Cpk-equivalent) computed on the Johnson-transformed scale.

machineMSAPro.outcome: Assesses a measurement system's (or machine's) bias and variation by comparing measured values against known reference/standard values, optionally by appraiser.
machineMSAPro.typicalQuestion: How much bias and variation does my measurement machine/system have relative to known standards?
machineMSAPro.dataType: Reference/standard value, measured value, optional appraiser/operator id, optional bias variable
machineMSAPro.predictorType: Measurement vs reference, optional appraiser grouping
machineMSAPro.resultMeaning: Bias and variation estimates for the machine/measurement system relative to the standard.

msaGageGoNogoPro.outcome: Validates a go/no-go (pass/fail) attribute gage by fitting a logistic regression of pass/fail outcome against a continuous reference measurement.
msaGageGoNogoPro.typicalQuestion: How well does my go/no-go gage agree with the true continuous measurement, and where is its effective threshold?
msaGageGoNogoPro.dataType: Continuous input measurement, binary pass/fail result
msaGageGoNogoPro.mainAssumptions: Binary response follows a logistic relationship with the continuous measurement
msaGageGoNogoPro.resultMeaning: A fitted logistic model characterizing the gage's pass/fail threshold and discrimination.

processCapabilityBenchmarkZNinePro.outcome: Computes BenchmarkZ ("nines") process capability metrics from pass/fail (good/bad) classification data.
processCapabilityBenchmarkZNinePro.typicalQuestion: How capable is my process, expressed as a BenchmarkZ ("nines") metric from pass/fail data?
processCapabilityBenchmarkZNinePro.dataType: A pass/good indicator variable and/or a fail/bad indicator variable
processCapabilityBenchmarkZNinePro.mainAssumptions: Pass/fail classifications reflect a stable underlying process
processCapabilityBenchmarkZNinePro.resultMeaning: A BenchmarkZ (nines) process capability metric derived from the pass/fail counts.

processCapabilityNonNormalPro.outcome: Performs process capability analysis for non-normally distributed data using an appropriate non-normal distribution fit.
processCapabilityNonNormalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I assess process capability when my data clearly isn't Normal, without transforming it first?
processCapabilityNonNormalPro.mainAssumptions: A suitable non-normal distribution can be fit to the data
processCapabilityNonNormalPro.resultMeaning: Process capability indices computed using the fitted non-normal distribution.

processCapabilityQccPro.outcome: Produces a "sixpack" process capability report (control charts, histogram, probability plot, and capability indices together) for one or more variables, optionally grouped.
processCapabilityQccPro.typicalQuestion: Can I get a full "sixpack" process capability report (charts + capability indices) in one view?
processCapabilityQccPro.dataType: Numeric variable(s) (observed process data), optional grouping variable
processCapabilityQccPro.mainAssumptions: Process is in statistical control for capability indices to be meaningful; Normality assumed unless otherwise specified
processCapabilityQccPro.resultMeaning: A combined sixpack report: control charts, histogram, probability plot, and capability indices.

regressionReliabilityLimitPro.dialog: Regression reliability limit analysis with censored and uncensored data
regressionReliabilityLimitPro.outcome: Fits a regression relating an input variable to a (possibly censored) reliability response, to estimate reliability limits.
regressionReliabilityLimitPro.typicalQuestion: How does an input factor (e.g. crimp diameter) affect a reliability outcome (e.g. burst pressure), accounting for censored observations?
regressionReliabilityLimitPro.dataType: Numeric response, numeric input, optional censoring indicator
regressionReliabilityLimitPro.mainAssumptions: Regression relationship holds; censoring mechanism is non-informative
regressionReliabilityLimitPro.resultMeaning: A fitted regression model with reliability limit estimates as a function of the input variable.

shewhartCharts1Pro.outcome: Plots Shewhart xbar/R or xbar/S control charts for subgrouped continuous process data.
shewhartCharts1Pro.typicalQuestion: Is my process's mean and variability in statistical control over time, using xbar/R or xbar/S charts?
shewhartCharts1Pro.mainAssumptions: Subgroups are rational (capture only common-cause variation within them)
shewhartCharts1Pro.resultMeaning: xbar and R/S control charts flagging any out-of-control subgroups.
