shewhartCharts2Pro.outcome: Plots Shewhart attribute control charts (p, np, c, or u) for defect/defective counts, optionally with varying sample sizes.
shewhartCharts2Pro.typicalQuestion: Is my process's defect or defective rate in statistical control over time?
shewhartCharts2Pro.mainAssumptions: Counts follow a binomial (p/np) or Poisson (c/u) process
shewhartCharts2Pro.resultMeaning: An attribute control chart flagging any out-of-control points.

shewhartCharts3Pro.outcome: Plots Individuals and Moving Range (I-MR) Shewhart control charts for individual continuous measurements (no subgrouping).
shewhartCharts3Pro.typicalQuestion: Is my process in statistical control when I only have one measurement per time period (individuals data)?
shewhartCharts3Pro.dataType: Numeric process variable, optional date variable for the x-axis
shewhartCharts3Pro.mainAssumptions: Consecutive individual observations are used to estimate short-term variation
shewhartCharts3Pro.resultMeaning: Individuals and Moving Range charts flagging any out-of-control points.

shewhartCharts4Pro.outcome: Plots Individuals and Moving Range control charts decomposed into between-subgroup and within-subgroup variation.
shewhartCharts4Pro.typicalQuestion: Is my process variation coming from between subgroups or within subgroups, using I-MR charts?
shewhartCharts4Pro.mainAssumptions: Subgroups are rational for separating between/within variation
shewhartCharts4Pro.resultMeaning: I-MR charts split into between- and within-subgroup components, flagging out-of-control signals in each.

strengthRegressionReliabilityPro.outcome: Fits a regression relating an input variable to a strength/capacity response, optionally by categorizing group, for reliability/strength analysis.
strengthRegressionReliabilityPro.typicalQuestion: How does an input factor affect strength/capacity, optionally across different categories/materials?
strengthRegressionReliabilityPro.dataType: Numeric response (strength), numeric input, categorizing variable
strengthRegressionReliabilityPro.mainAssumptions: Regression relationship holds within each category
strengthRegressionReliabilityPro.resultMeaning: A fitted regression model relating input to strength/capacity, optionally per category.

stressVsStrengthReliabilityPro.outcome: Estimates reliability (probability that strength exceeds stress) by comparing the distributions of a strength variable and a stress/load variable.
stressVsStrengthReliabilityPro.typicalQuestion: What is the probability that my component's strength exceeds the stress it will experience?
stressVsStrengthReliabilityPro.dataType: Numeric strength/capacity variable, numeric stress/load variable
stressVsStrengthReliabilityPro.mainAssumptions: Strength and stress distributions are estimated accurately from the given data
stressVsStrengthReliabilityPro.resultMeaning: An estimated reliability (probability strength exceeds stress) based on the two distributions.

toleranceIntervalsPro.outcome: Computes a statistical tolerance interval - a range expected to contain a specified proportion of the population with a given confidence - for a numeric variable.
toleranceIntervalsPro.typicalQuestion: What range should contain a specified percentage of my population, with a given confidence level?
toleranceIntervalsPro.mainAssumptions: Data follows the assumed distribution (commonly Normal) used for the tolerance interval calculation
toleranceIntervalsPro.resultMeaning: A tolerance interval expected to contain the specified population proportion at the given confidence level.

AIC.outcome: Computes the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) for an already-fitted model, to help compare model fit while penalizing complexity.
AIC.typicalQuestion: What is my fitted model's AIC?
AIC.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
AIC.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
AIC.resultMeaning: The model's AIC value (lower generally indicates better fit relative to complexity).

BIC.outcome: Computes the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) for an already-fitted model, to help compare model fit while penalizing complexity.
BIC.typicalQuestion: What is my fitted model's BIC?
BIC.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
BIC.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
BIC.resultMeaning: The model's BIC value (lower generally indicates better fit relative to complexity, with a stronger complexity penalty than AIC).

EmmeansPredictionPlot.outcome: Plots estimated marginal means (predicted values holding other predictors at reference levels) from an already-fitted model across one or more numeric predictors and a grouping variable.
EmmeansPredictionPlot.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize predicted/estimated marginal means from my fitted model across a predictor and group?
EmmeansPredictionPlot.dataType: Numeric predictor variable(s), grouping variable(s) - referencing an already-fitted model
EmmeansPredictionPlot.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit; emmeans holds unlisted predictors at reference/average values
EmmeansPredictionPlot.resultMeaning: A plot of estimated marginal means (typically with confidence bands) across the chosen predictor and group.

iCCPlots.outcome: Plots item characteristic curves (ICCs) for an already-fitted item response theory (IRT) model.
iCCPlots.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize item characteristic curves for my fitted IRT model?
iCCPlots.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted IRT model
iCCPlots.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
iCCPlots.resultMeaning: Item characteristic curve plots showing each item's response probability across ability levels.

itemAndTestInfo.outcome: Computes/plots item and test information functions for an already-fitted item response theory (IRT) model.
itemAndTestInfo.typicalQuestion: How much statistical information do my test items provide across the ability range?
itemAndTestInfo.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted IRT model
itemAndTestInfo.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
itemAndTestInfo.resultMeaning: Item and test information functions/plots, showing where the test measures most precisely.

itemFit.outcome: Assesses how well individual items fit an already-fitted item response theory (IRT) model.
itemFit.typicalQuestion: Do my test items fit my fitted IRT model well?
itemFit.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted IRT model
itemFit.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
itemFit.resultMeaning: Item-level fit statistics flagging items that don't fit the IRT model well.

likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.outcome: Computes likelihood ratio tests and plots item discrimination (beta) parameters for an already-fitted IRT model.
likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.typicalQuestion: How do I test and visualize item discrimination parameters for my fitted IRT model?
likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.dataType: Variables (items) to plot betas for, from an already-fitted IRT model
likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.predictorType: N/A - operates on a fitted model's items
likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
likelihoodRatiosPlotBetas.resultMeaning: Likelihood ratio test results and a plot of item beta (discrimination) parameters.

personFit.outcome: Assesses how well individual respondents' response patterns fit an already-fitted IRT model, via person-fit statistics and Martin-Löf's test.
personFit.typicalQuestion: Which respondents have unusual/misfitting response patterns under my fitted IRT model?
personFit.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted IRT model
personFit.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
personFit.resultMeaning: Person-fit statistics flagging respondents whose response patterns don't fit the model well.

plotPImap.outcome: Plots a person-item map showing the distribution of respondent ability alongside item difficulty for an already-fitted IRT model.
plotPImap.typicalQuestion: How do respondent ability and item difficulty compare on the same scale, for my fitted IRT model?
plotPImap.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted IRT model
plotPImap.mainAssumptions: An IRT model has already been fit
plotPImap.resultMeaning: A person-item map placing respondent ability and item difficulty on a shared scale.

Scoring.dialog: Score A Dataset Using A Model
Scoring.outcome: Applies an already-fitted model to a dataset to generate predicted values/scores for each observation.
Scoring.typicalQuestion: How do I use my fitted model to generate predictions/scores for a dataset?
Scoring.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model and a target dataset
Scoring.mainAssumptions: The target dataset has the same predictor variables the model was fit with
Scoring.resultMeaning: The dataset with new predicted score/value column(s) added from the model.

scoringSurvivalCL.outcome: Applies an already-fitted Cox survival model to generate predicted survival probabilities for a dataset.
scoringSurvivalCL.typicalQuestion: How do I get predicted survival probabilities from my fitted Cox model for new observations?
scoringSurvivalCL.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted Cox model and a target dataset
scoringSurvivalCL.mainAssumptions: The target dataset has the same predictor variables the Cox model was fit with
scoringSurvivalCL.resultMeaning: Predicted survival probabilities added to the target dataset.

scoringSurvivalML.dialog: Score a dataset using a Survival Model
scoringSurvivalML.outcome: Applies an already-fitted parametric survival model to generate predicted values/scores for a dataset.
scoringSurvivalML.typicalQuestion: How do I score a dataset using my fitted parametric survival model?
scoringSurvivalML.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted survival model and a target dataset (all its variables must be present)
scoringSurvivalML.mainAssumptions: The target dataset has all the variables the survival model was fit with
scoringSurvivalML.resultMeaning: The dataset with new predicted survival score/value column(s) added.

addStatisticsToObservations.outcome: Adds observation-level model statistics (e.g. fitted values, residuals, leverage) from an already-fitted model back onto the original dataset.
addStatisticsToObservations.typicalQuestion: How do I add my fitted model's residuals/fitted values/diagnostics back onto my dataset as new columns?
addStatisticsToObservations.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model and its source dataset
addStatisticsToObservations.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit on the dataset in question
addStatisticsToObservations.resultMeaning: The dataset with new columns for the requested model statistics.

anovaLikelihoodRatio.outcome: Compares nested already-fitted models using an ANOVA-style or likelihood ratio test.
anovaLikelihoodRatio.typicalQuestion: Does adding these extra terms to my model significantly improve fit (nested model comparison)?
anovaLikelihoodRatio.mainAssumptions: The models being compared are nested (one is a special case of the other)
anovaLikelihoodRatio.resultMeaning: A test statistic/p-value for whether the more complex model fits significantly better.

bonFerroniOutlierTest.outcome: Tests for outlying observations in an already-fitted regression model using the Bonferroni-corrected outlier test on studentized residuals.
bonFerroniOutlierTest.typicalQuestion: Does my fitted regression model have any statistically significant outliers?
bonFerroniOutlierTest.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted regression model
bonFerroniOutlierTest.mainAssumptions: A regression model has already been fit
bonFerroniOutlierTest.resultMeaning: The observation(s), if any, flagged as significant outliers after Bonferroni correction.

compareModels.outcome: Compares two nested already-fitted models using an F or Chi-square likelihood ratio test.
compareModels.typicalQuestion: Does my fuller model fit significantly better than a simpler nested version of it?
compareModels.dataType: N/A - operates on two already-fitted (nested) models
compareModels.mainAssumptions: The two models are nested (one's terms are a subset of the other's), from supported model classes (lm, glm, lme, polr, coxph, gls, survreg, loess, nls, multinom - not models from Model Tuning)
compareModels.resultMeaning: A test statistic/p-value for whether the fuller model fits significantly better than the reduced model.

compareNModels.outcome: Compares performance/fit statistics across N already-fitted models side by side.
compareNModels.typicalQuestion: How do several of my fitted models compare to each other on fit statistics?
compareNModels.dataType: N/A - operates on multiple already-fitted models
compareNModels.mainAssumptions: Multiple models have already been fit
compareNModels.resultMeaning: A side-by-side comparison table of fit statistics across the selected models.

compareNModelsSEM.outcome: Compares fit statistics across N already-fitted structural equation models (SEM).
compareNModelsSEM.typicalQuestion: How do several of my fitted SEM models compare on fit indices?
compareNModelsSEM.dataType: N/A - operates on multiple already-fitted SEM models
compareNModelsSEM.mainAssumptions: Multiple SEM models have already been fit
compareNModelsSEM.resultMeaning: A side-by-side comparison table of SEM fit indices across the selected models.

compareQuantReg.outcome: Tests whether slopes differ significantly across multiple already-fitted quantile regression models (e.g. across quantiles).
compareQuantReg.typicalQuestion: Do my quantile regression slopes differ significantly across quantiles/models?
compareQuantReg.dataType: N/A - operates on multiple already-fitted quantile regression models
compareQuantReg.mainAssumptions: Multiple quantile regression models have already been fit on comparable data
compareQuantReg.resultMeaning: A test of whether slope coefficients differ significantly across the compared quantile models.

confidenceInterval.outcome: Computes confidence intervals for the coefficients of an already-fitted model.
confidenceInterval.typicalQuestion: What are the confidence intervals for my fitted model's coefficients?
confidenceInterval.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
confidenceInterval.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
confidenceInterval.resultMeaning: Confidence intervals for each coefficient in the fitted model.

convertNModelsRSMtoLM.dialog: Convert N Models from RSM terms (if any) to expanded terms
convertNModelsRSMtoLM.outcome: Converts one or more already-fitted response surface (RSM) models' compact term notation into expanded linear-model terms for further use/comparison.
convertNModelsRSMtoLM.typicalQuestion: How do I convert my RSM model's compact terms into an expanded linear-model form?
convertNModelsRSMtoLM.dataType: N/A - operates on already-fitted RSM models
convertNModelsRSMtoLM.mainAssumptions: The model(s) were fit as RSM models with convertible term notation
convertNModelsRSMtoLM.resultMeaning: New companion model object(s) with terms expanded into standard linear-model form.

deleteNModels.outcome: Deletes one or more already-fitted model objects from the current session.
deleteNModels.typicalQuestion: How do I remove a fitted model I no longer need?
deleteNModels.dataType: N/A - operates on already-fitted model objects
deleteNModels.mainAssumptions: One or more models have already been fit
deleteNModels.resultMeaning: The selected model object(s) are removed from the session.

hosmerLemeshow.outcome: Tests the goodness-of-fit of an already-fitted logistic regression model using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test.
hosmerLemeshow.typicalQuestion: Does my fitted logistic regression model fit the data well, per the Hosmer-Lemeshow test?
hosmerLemeshow.dataType: Target/outcome variable, from an already-fitted logistic model
hosmerLemeshow.mainAssumptions: A logistic regression model has already been fit
hosmerLemeshow.resultMeaning: A Hosmer-Lemeshow test statistic/p-value assessing overall model calibration.

modelLevelStatistics.outcome: Displays overall (model-level) fit statistics for an already-fitted model.
modelLevelStatistics.typicalQuestion: What are the overall fit statistics (R-squared, deviance, etc.) for my fitted model?
modelLevelStatistics.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
modelLevelStatistics.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
modelLevelStatistics.resultMeaning: A table of model-level fit statistics.

parameterLevelStats.outcome: Displays parameter (coefficient)-level estimates and statistics for an already-fitted model.
parameterLevelStats.typicalQuestion: What are my fitted model's coefficient estimates, standard errors, and significance?
parameterLevelStats.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
parameterLevelStats.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
parameterLevelStats.resultMeaning: A table of coefficient-level estimates, standard errors, test statistics, and p-values.

plotAModel.outcome: Produces diagnostic or effect plots for an already-fitted model.
plotAModel.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize/plot a model I already fit?
plotAModel.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
plotAModel.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit

pseudoRSquared.outcome: Computes a pseudo R-squared statistic for an already-fitted model (e.g. logistic, GLM) that doesn't have a standard R-squared.
pseudoRSquared.typicalQuestion: What's the pseudo R-squared for my fitted logistic/GLM model?
pseudoRSquared.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
pseudoRSquared.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
pseudoRSquared.resultMeaning: A pseudo R-squared value estimating the model's explanatory power.

stepwise.outcome: Performs stepwise (forward/backward/both) variable selection starting from an already-fitted model.
stepwise.typicalQuestion: How do I do stepwise variable selection on my fitted model?
stepwise.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
stepwise.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit; stepwise selection has known limitations (e.g. inflated Type I error) worth flagging to the user
stepwise.resultMeaning: A refined model with variables selected via the stepwise procedure.

summarizeAModel.outcome: Produces a standard summary (coefficients, fit statistics) for an already-fitted model.
summarizeAModel.typicalQuestion: How do I get a standard summary of my fitted model?
summarizeAModel.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
summarizeAModel.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
summarizeAModel.resultMeaning: A standard summary of the fitted model's coefficients and fit statistics.

summarizeNModels.outcome: Produces standard summaries for multiple already-fitted models side by side.
summarizeNModels.typicalQuestion: How do I get summaries for several of my fitted models at once?
summarizeNModels.dataType: N/A - operates on multiple already-fitted models
summarizeNModels.mainAssumptions: Multiple models have already been fit
summarizeNModels.resultMeaning: Side-by-side standard summaries for each selected model.

varianceInflationFactors.outcome: Computes variance inflation factors (VIF) for an already-fitted regression model's predictors, to assess multicollinearity.
varianceInflationFactors.typicalQuestion: Is there problematic multicollinearity among my fitted regression model's predictors?
varianceInflationFactors.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted regression model
varianceInflationFactors.mainAssumptions: A regression model has already been fit with 2+ predictors
varianceInflationFactors.resultMeaning: VIF values per predictor - high values (commonly >5 or >10) flag problematic multicollinearity.

CatAgree.outcome: Measures agreement among two or more raters classifying items into categories.
CatAgree.typicalQuestion: Do multiple raters agree when classifying items into categories?
CatAgree.pairedIndependent: Repeated (same items rated by each rater)
CatAgree.mainAssumptions: Categories are mutually exclusive and consistently defined
CatAgree.resultMeaning: An agreement statistic (e.g. kappa-type) summarizing rater agreement.

CompetingRisksCompareGroups.outcome: Estimates and compares cumulative incidence of competing risks (multiple distinct event types) across groups.
CompetingRisksCompareGroups.typicalQuestion: How does the risk of one event type (among several competing event types) compare across groups?
CompetingRisksCompareGroups.dataType: Time-to-event, multi-level event indicator (competing risks), grouping variable
CompetingRisksCompareGroups.mainAssumptions: Competing events are correctly coded; censoring is non-informative
CompetingRisksCompareGroups.resultMeaning: Cumulative incidence curves/tests comparing competing-risk probabilities across groups.

ConditionalLogistic.outcome: Fits a conditional logistic regression model for matched case-control data, conditioning on strata.
ConditionalLogistic.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a logistic regression for matched case-control data (e.g. 1:1 or 1:N matched pairs)?
ConditionalLogistic.dataType: Binary (event/no event) dependent variable, stratum (matching) variable, predictors via formula
ConditionalLogistic.mainAssumptions: Matching strata correctly group cases with their matched controls
ConditionalLogistic.resultMeaning: Conditional logistic coefficient estimates (odds ratios) accounting for the matched design.

CoxFineGray.outcome: Fits a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model for competing-risks time-to-event data.
CoxFineGray.typicalQuestion: How do I model the risk of one event type when competing risks (other event types) are present?
CoxFineGray.dataType: Time-to-event, multi-level event indicator (competing risks), optional stratification/weights
CoxFineGray.mainAssumptions: Proportional subdistribution hazards; competing events correctly coded
CoxFineGray.resultMeaning: Subdistribution hazard ratio estimates for the event of interest, accounting for competing risks.

CoxRegMultiple.outcome: Fits multiple Cox proportional-hazards models at once, each adding a different set of adjustment variables to a base model, for sensitivity/adjustment comparison.
CoxRegMultiple.typicalQuestion: How does my Cox model's effect estimate change as I add different sets of adjustment variables?
CoxRegMultiple.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, independent variable(s), up to 5 sets of adjustment variables, optional strata/weights
CoxRegMultiple.predictorType: Time (dependent), event status, independent variables, adjustment sets
CoxRegMultiple.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards for each fitted model
CoxRegMultiple.resultMeaning: A series of Cox models showing how estimates change across the specified adjustment sets.

CoxStratified.outcome: Fits a Cox proportional-hazards model stratified by one or more variables, allowing the baseline hazard to differ across strata.
CoxStratified.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a Cox model that allows a different baseline hazard across strata (e.g. study site)?
CoxStratified.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, stratification variable(s), optional weights
CoxStratified.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards within each stratum (baseline hazard can differ across strata)
CoxStratified.resultMeaning: Hazard ratio estimates common across strata, with stratum-specific baseline hazards.

CoxTimeDependent.outcome: Fits a Cox model with binary time-dependent covariates (exposure that starts partway through follow-up), using exposure-time variables and subject id.
CoxTimeDependent.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a Cox model when a covariate's value can change partway through follow-up (e.g. treatment starts later)?
CoxTimeDependent.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, exposure-time variable(s), subject identifier, optional weights
CoxTimeDependent.predictorType: Time (dependent), event status, time-dependent exposure, subject
CoxTimeDependent.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; exposure timing is accurately recorded
CoxTimeDependent.resultMeaning: Hazard ratio estimates accounting for the time-varying exposure.

CrosstabList.outcome: Produces a list-format crosstab (long table of category combinations and counts) for multiple categorical variables.
CrosstabList.typicalQuestion: How do I get a crosstab of several categorical variables in a list/long format rather than a wide table?
CrosstabList.resultMeaning: A long-format table of category combinations and their counts/percentages.

DateOrderCheck.outcome: Checks that a set of date variables occur in the expected chronological order within each row, flagging violations.
DateOrderCheck.typicalQuestion: Are my date variables (e.g. enrollment, treatment, follow-up dates) in the correct chronological order for each subject?
DateOrderCheck.dataType: Two or more date variables of the same class, optional row-identification variable(s)
DateOrderCheck.mainAssumptions: Dates are entered in a comparable format/class
DateOrderCheck.resultMeaning: A report flagging rows where the specified dates are out of the expected order.

ExploreDataset.outcome: Provides an interactive overview/exploration of a dataset's variables, types, and basic statistics.
ExploreDataset.typicalQuestion: How do I get a quick interactive overview of everything in my dataset?
ExploreDataset.resultMeaning: An interactive summary/overview of the dataset's structure and variables.

FillValuesDownwardUpward.outcome: Fills missing values in a variable by carrying the last (or next) non-missing value forward or backward, optionally within groups.
FillValuesDownwardUpward.typicalQuestion: How do I fill in missing values by carrying forward (or backward) the last known value, e.g. within each subject?
FillValuesDownwardUpward.dataType: Any variable(s) with missing values, optional grouping variable(s)
FillValuesDownwardUpward.mainAssumptions: Last-observation-carried-forward/backward is a reasonable assumption for the missingness pattern
FillValuesDownwardUpward.resultMeaning: The variable(s) with missing values filled in from the nearest non-missing value in the specified direction.

ForestPlot.outcome: Plots effect estimates (e.g. hazard/odds ratios) with confidence intervals for one or more variables from an already-fitted model, as a forest plot.
ForestPlot.typicalQuestion: How do I visualize my model's effect estimates and confidence intervals as a forest plot?
ForestPlot.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted model
ForestPlot.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit
ForestPlot.resultMeaning: A forest plot of effect estimates and confidence intervals for the selected (or all) model terms.

GraphExplorerPro.outcome: Provides an interactive graph-building interface for exploring a dataset visually across multiple chart types.
GraphExplorerPro.typicalQuestion: How do I interactively build and explore different chart types for my dataset?
GraphExplorerPro.resultMeaning: An interactive graph exploration interface for the selected dataset.

LinearRegMultiple.outcome: Fits multiple linear regression models at once, each adding a different set of adjustment variables to a base model, for sensitivity/adjustment comparison.
LinearRegMultiple.typicalQuestion: How does my linear regression estimate change as I add different sets of adjustment variables?
LinearRegMultiple.dataType: Numeric dependent variable, independent variable(s), up to 5 sets of adjustment variables, optional strata/weights
LinearRegMultiple.mainAssumptions: Standard linear regression assumptions for each fitted model
LinearRegMultiple.resultMeaning: A series of linear models showing how estimates change across the specified adjustment sets.

LogisticRegMultiple.outcome: Fits multiple logistic regression models at once, each adding a different set of adjustment variables to a base model, for sensitivity/adjustment comparison.
LogisticRegMultiple.typicalQuestion: How does my logistic regression's odds ratio change as I add different sets of adjustment variables?
LogisticRegMultiple.dataType: Binary/categorical dependent variable, independent variable(s), up to 5 sets of adjustment variables, optional strata/weights
LogisticRegMultiple.mainAssumptions: Standard logistic regression assumptions for each fitted model
LogisticRegMultiple.resultMeaning: A series of logistic models showing how odds-ratio estimates change across the specified adjustment sets.

OddsRatioRelativeRisk.dialog: Odds Ratios / Relative Risks, M by 2 Table
OddsRatioRelativeRisk.outcome: Computes odds ratios and relative risks for an outcome across multiple levels of an exposure/predictor variable (M-by-2 table).
OddsRatioRelativeRisk.typicalQuestion: What are the odds ratios / relative risks for my outcome across levels of an exposure variable?
OddsRatioRelativeRisk.dataType: Binary outcome variable, categorical exposure/predictor variable (2+ levels)
OddsRatioRelativeRisk.resultMeaning: Odds ratios and relative risks (with confidence intervals) for each exposure level vs a reference.

RiskSetMatching.outcome: Matches cases to controls from the risk set at the time of each event, based on specified matching variables, for case-control or nested case-control designs.
RiskSetMatching.typicalQuestion: How do I match cases to controls from the appropriate risk set at each event time?
RiskSetMatching.dataType: Event indicator, time variable, numeric matching variable(s)
RiskSetMatching.mainAssumptions: Matching variables are meaningful for balancing cases and controls
RiskSetMatching.resultMeaning: A new dataset of matched case-control sets drawn from the risk set at each event time.

Separate.outcome: Splits a single variable's values (e.g. a delimited string) into multiple new variables.
Separate.typicalQuestion: How do I split one column of combined values into several separate columns?
Separate.dataType: A character/string variable containing combinable/delimited values
Separate.mainAssumptions: The variable's values follow a consistent, splittable pattern
Separate.resultMeaning: New variables created from splitting the original variable's values.

SubjectMatching.outcome: Matches case subjects to control subjects using exact and/or caliper (numeric tolerance) matching on specified variables.
SubjectMatching.typicalQuestion: How do I match my case subjects to control subjects on specific characteristics?
SubjectMatching.dataType: Case/control indicator variable, optional exact-matching variables, optional caliper (numeric tolerance) matching variables
SubjectMatching.mainAssumptions: Matching variables are meaningful confounders/covariates to balance
SubjectMatching.resultMeaning: A new dataset of matched case-control pairs/sets.

SubsetByLogic.outcome: Creates a new dataset containing only rows matching a specified logical condition, and optionally only selected variables.
SubsetByLogic.typicalQuestion: How do I subset my dataset to only rows matching a custom logical condition?
SubsetByLogic.dataType: Any (variables used in the logical condition and/or to keep)
SubsetByLogic.resultMeaning: A new dataset containing only the rows (and optionally variables) matching the specified logic.

UpdateMerge.outcome: Merges an update/correction dataset into an existing dataset, overwriting matching rows/columns with the updated values.
UpdateMerge.typicalQuestion: How do I apply an update dataset (corrections/new values) onto my existing dataset?
UpdateMerge.dataType: Two datasets sharing a matching key
UpdateMerge.mainAssumptions: The datasets share a meaningful key for matching rows to update
UpdateMerge.resultMeaning: The original dataset with matching rows/values updated from the update dataset.

ccc.outcome: Measures agreement between two continuous observers/methods using the concordance correlation coefficient (accounting for both precision and accuracy).
ccc.typicalQuestion: How well do two continuous measurement methods/observers agree, accounting for both correlation and systematic bias?
ccc.mainAssumptions: Measurements are paired and on the same scale
ccc.resultMeaning: A concordance correlation coefficient summarizing agreement between the two observers.

cccmult.outcome: Measures agreement among three or more continuous raters/observers using a multi-rater concordance correlation coefficient.
cccmult.typicalQuestion: How well do three or more continuous measurement methods/observers agree with each other?
cccmult.dataType: Three or more numeric/scale rater variables
cccmult.pairedIndependent: Repeated (same items rated by each rater)
cccmult.mainAssumptions: Measurements are on the same scale across raters
cccmult.resultMeaning: A multi-rater concordance correlation coefficient summarizing overall agreement.

enetCoxPro.outcome: Fits a regularized (elastic net) Cox proportional-hazards model, useful for variable selection with many predictors.
enetCoxPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a Cox survival model with regularization/variable selection when I have many predictors?
enetCoxPro.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, many independent variables, optional offset/weights/strata
enetCoxPro.mainAssumptions: Proportional hazards; regularization penalty appropriately tuned
enetCoxPro.resultMeaning: A regularized Cox model with a subset of predictors selected/shrunk by the elastic net penalty.

enetPro.outcome: Fits a regularized (elastic net) regression model, useful for variable selection and multicollinearity when there are many predictors.
enetPro.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a regression with regularization/variable selection when I have many (possibly correlated) predictors?
enetPro.dataType: Numeric/categorical dependent variable, many independent variables, optional offset/weights
enetPro.resultMeaning: A regularized model with a subset of predictors selected/shrunk by the elastic net penalty.

geeMultinomialPro.outcome: Fits a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model for a multinomial (multi-category) dependent variable with clustered/repeated data.
geeMultinomialPro.typicalQuestion: How do I model a multi-category outcome with clustered/repeated observations (e.g. multiple measurements per subject)?
geeMultinomialPro.dataType: Multinomial (categorical, 3+ level) dependent variable, cluster identifier, optional within-cluster order, optional offset
geeMultinomialPro.mainAssumptions: Correct specification of the working correlation structure within clusters (GEE is robust to misspecification for point estimates)
geeMultinomialPro.resultMeaning: Population-averaged coefficient estimates accounting for within-cluster correlation.

geeOrdinalPro.outcome: Fits a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model for an ordinal (ordered categorical) dependent variable with clustered/repeated data.
geeOrdinalPro.typicalQuestion: How do I model an ordered categorical outcome with clustered/repeated observations?
geeOrdinalPro.dataType: Ordinal dependent variable, cluster identifier, optional within-cluster order, optional offset
geeOrdinalPro.mainAssumptions: Correct specification of the working correlation structure within clusters
geeOrdinalPro.resultMeaning: Population-averaged coefficient estimates accounting for within-cluster correlation.

geePro.outcome: Fits a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model for clustered/repeated-measures data with a general (e.g. continuous, binary, count) dependent variable.
geePro.typicalQuestion: How do I model a repeated-measures/clustered outcome accounting for within-subject correlation?
geePro.dataType: Dependent variable, cluster identifier, optional within-cluster ordering/spacing, optional offset/weights
geePro.mainAssumptions: Correct specification of the working correlation structure within clusters
geePro.resultMeaning: Population-averaged coefficient estimates accounting for within-cluster correlation.

modelContrastsMaineffectPro.outcome: Computes all pairwise contrasts (comparisons) among the levels of specified model terms from an already-fitted model.
modelContrastsMaineffectPro.typicalQuestion: How do all pairs of factor levels in my fitted model compare to each other?
modelContrastsMaineffectPro.dataType: Variables (factor terms) to compute all pairwise contrasts for, from an already-fitted model
modelContrastsMaineffectPro.mainAssumptions: A model has already been fit including the specified factor(s)
modelContrastsMaineffectPro.resultMeaning: A table of all pairwise comparisons among factor levels, with estimates and adjusted p-values.

movevars.outcome: Reorders specific variables in the dataset, moving them to a new position (e.g. after a specified variable).
movevars.typicalQuestion: How do I move specific columns to a different position in my dataset?
movevars.resultMeaning: The dataset's columns reordered with the selected variables moved to the specified position.

parametricSurvivalRegression.outcome: Fits a parametric survival regression model (e.g. Weibull, lognormal AFT) relating predictors to time-to-event.
parametricSurvivalRegression.typicalQuestion: How do I fit a parametric (not semi-parametric Cox) survival regression model with predictors?
parametricSurvivalRegression.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, independent variables, optional weights
parametricSurvivalRegression.mainAssumptions: The chosen parametric distribution fits the failure-time data; censoring is non-informative
parametricSurvivalRegression.resultMeaning: A fitted parametric survival regression model with coefficient/time-ratio estimates.

rocTdComparePro.outcome: Compares time-dependent ROC curves for two or more markers predicting a time-to-event outcome.
rocTdComparePro.typicalQuestion: Which of my markers better predicts a time-to-event outcome, using time-dependent ROC comparison?
rocTdComparePro.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, two or more numeric markers
rocTdComparePro.mainAssumptions: Higher marker values correspond to higher event risk; censoring is non-informative
rocTdComparePro.resultMeaning: Time-dependent ROC curves and a comparison of predictive performance across markers.

rocTdCompriskComparePro.dialog: Compare ROC Curves, time-dependent competing risks
rocTdCompriskComparePro.outcome: Compares time-dependent ROC curves for two or more markers predicting a specific event type in the presence of competing risks.
rocTdCompriskComparePro.typicalQuestion: Which of my markers better predicts a specific event type when competing risks are present?
rocTdCompriskComparePro.dataType: Time-to-event, multi-level event indicator (competing risks), two or more numeric markers
rocTdCompriskComparePro.mainAssumptions: Higher marker values correspond to higher event risk; competing events correctly coded
rocTdCompriskComparePro.resultMeaning: Time-dependent ROC curves and a comparison of predictive performance across markers, accounting for competing risks.

rocTdCompriskPro.outcome: Computes a time-dependent ROC curve for a marker predicting a specific event type in the presence of competing risks.
rocTdCompriskPro.typicalQuestion: How well does my marker predict a specific event type over time, when competing risks are present?
rocTdCompriskPro.dataType: Time-to-event, multi-level event indicator (competing risks), one numeric marker
rocTdCompriskPro.mainAssumptions: Higher marker values correspond to higher event risk; competing events correctly coded
rocTdCompriskPro.resultMeaning: A time-dependent ROC curve and AUC for the marker's predictive performance, accounting for competing risks.

rocTdPro.outcome: Computes a time-dependent ROC curve for a marker predicting a time-to-event outcome.
rocTdPro.typicalQuestion: How well does my marker predict a time-to-event outcome, evaluated over time?
rocTdPro.dataType: Time-to-event, event indicator, one numeric marker
rocTdPro.mainAssumptions: Higher marker values correspond to higher event risk; censoring is non-informative
rocTdPro.resultMeaning: A time-dependent ROC curve and AUC for the marker's predictive performance.

scoringParametricSurvival.outcome: Applies an already-fitted parametric survival model to generate predicted survival probabilities for a dataset.
scoringParametricSurvival.typicalQuestion: How do I get predicted survival probabilities from my fitted parametric survival model for new observations?
scoringParametricSurvival.dataType: N/A - operates on an already-fitted parametric survival model and a target dataset
scoringParametricSurvival.mainAssumptions: The target dataset has the same predictor variables the survival model was fit with
scoringParametricSurvival.resultMeaning: Predicted survival probabilities added to the target dataset.

ConvertToOrdinal.outcome: Converts one or more variables into ordered factors (ordinal), with a specified level order.
ConvertToOrdinal.typicalQuestion: How do I convert a variable into an ordered factor (ordinal), with levels in a specific order?
ConvertToOrdinal.resultMeaning: The variable(s) converted to ordered factor (ordinal) type.

addNewLevels.outcome: Adds new (currently unused) levels to one or more factor variables.
addNewLevels.typicalQuestion: How do I add a new possible level/category to a factor variable, even if no rows currently use it?
addNewLevels.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s) gain the specified new level(s).

addRemoveBoxCoxLambda.dialog: Add/Replace/Remove Lambda (λ) for a variable with prior Box-Cox transformation
addRemoveBoxCoxLambda.outcome: Manually sets, replaces, or removes the stored Box-Cox lambda associated with a variable.
addRemoveBoxCoxLambda.typicalQuestion: How do I manually set or clear the Box-Cox lambda stored for a variable?
addRemoveBoxCoxLambda.resultMeaning: The variable's stored Box-Cox lambda is added, replaced, or removed.

applyFunctionAcrossRows.dialog: Applying a function to all rows of selected variable(s).
applyFunctionAcrossRows.outcome: Applies a specified function (e.g. sum, mean, max) across the selected variables for each row, creating a new variable.
applyFunctionAcrossRows.typicalQuestion: How do I compute a row-wise function (e.g. sum, mean) across several variables?
applyFunctionAcrossRows.mainAssumptions: The selected variables are compatible for the chosen row-wise function
applyFunctionAcrossRows.resultMeaning: A new variable containing the row-wise function result across the selected variables.

binNumericVariables.outcome: Bins (discretizes) a numeric variable into categorical intervals/groups.
binNumericVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I bin/discretize a continuous variable into categories (e.g. age groups)?
binNumericVariables.mainAssumptions: Bin boundaries/counts chosen are meaningful for the analysis
binNumericVariables.resultMeaning: A new categorical (binned) variable derived from the numeric variable.

byAnotherVariable.dialog: Reorder Factor Levels by Another Variable
byAnotherVariable.outcome: Reorders a factor variable's levels based on the values of another (typically numeric) variable.
byAnotherVariable.typicalQuestion: How do I reorder a factor's levels based on another variable's values (e.g. order by mean of a numeric variable)?
byAnotherVariable.dataType: Factor variable to reorder, an ordering variable
byAnotherVariable.mainAssumptions: The ordering variable meaningfully relates to the factor's levels
byAnotherVariable.resultMeaning: The factor variable's levels reordered according to the specified ordering variable.

computeDummyVariables.outcome: Creates dummy (0/1 indicator) variables for the levels of one or more categorical variables.
computeDummyVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I create dummy/indicator variables from a categorical variable, e.g. for use in a model?
computeDummyVariables.resultMeaning: New 0/1 dummy variables, one per level of the selected categorical variable(s).

computeVariable.outcome: Creates a new variable computed from an arbitrary user-specified expression involving existing variables.
computeVariable.typicalQuestion: How do I create a new variable using a custom formula/expression?
computeVariable.mainAssumptions: The specified expression is valid R syntax
computeVariable.resultMeaning: A new variable containing the result of the specified expression.

concatenateVariables.outcome: Concatenates (joins) the values of two or more variables into a single new character variable.
concatenateVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I combine several columns' values into one text column?
concatenateVariables.resultMeaning: A new character variable with the concatenated values of the selected variables.

conditionalCompute.outcome: Creates a new variable whose value depends on a specified logical condition (if/else-style computation).
conditionalCompute.typicalQuestion: How do I create a variable whose value depends on a condition (e.g. if X > 10 then "high" else "low")?
conditionalCompute.resultMeaning: A new variable with values determined by the specified condition.

conditionalComputeMayo.outcome: Creates a new variable whose value depends on multiple specified logical conditions (if/elseif/else-style computation across several rules).
conditionalComputeMayo.typicalQuestion: How do I create a variable with several conditional rules (like a multi-branch if/elseif/else)?
conditionalComputeMayo.resultMeaning: A new variable with values determined by the first matching condition among the specified rules.

convertDateToString.outcome: Converts one or more date variables into character (text) variables.
convertDateToString.typicalQuestion: How do I convert a date column into text?
convertDateToString.resultMeaning: The date variable(s) converted to character type.

convertNumericToDate.outcome: Converts a numeric variable (e.g. Excel/Unix date serial number) into a proper date/time variable.
convertNumericToDate.typicalQuestion: How do I convert a numeric date code (e.g. from Excel) into an actual date variable?
convertNumericToDate.dataType: Numeric variable representing a date/time serial value
convertNumericToDate.mainAssumptions: The numeric values follow a known date/time serial convention
convertNumericToDate.resultMeaning: A new date/time variable converted from the numeric values.

convertStringToDate.outcome: Converts a character (text) variable into a date/time variable, given its format.
convertStringToDate.typicalQuestion: How do I convert a text column (e.g. "2024-01-15") into an actual date variable?
convertStringToDate.mainAssumptions: The text follows a consistent, specifiable date format
convertStringToDate.resultMeaning: A new date/time variable converted from the character values.

convertStringToDateTime.dialog: Convert Character Variables To Date & Time
convertStringToDateTime.outcome: Converts one or more character (text) variables into date/time variables, given their format.
convertStringToDateTime.typicalQuestion: How do I convert several text columns into date/time variables at once?
convertStringToDateTime.mainAssumptions: The text follows a consistent, specifiable date/time format
convertStringToDateTime.resultMeaning: New date/time variable(s) converted from the character values.

convertToFactor.outcome: Converts one or more variables into (unordered) factor type.
convertToFactor.typicalQuestion: How do I convert a variable into a factor/categorical type?
convertToFactor.resultMeaning: The variable(s) converted to (unordered) factor type.

deleteVariables.outcome: Deletes one or more variables from the dataset.
deleteVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I delete a column/variable from my dataset?
deleteVariables.resultMeaning: The selected variable(s) are removed from the dataset.

displayLevels.outcome: Displays the current levels (in order) of one or more factor variables.
displayLevels.typicalQuestion: What are the current levels (and their order) of my factor variable?
displayLevels.resultMeaning: A listing of each selected factor variable's current levels and order.

dropUnusedLevels.outcome: Removes factor levels that have no observations remaining (e.g. after subsetting) from one or more factor variables.
dropUnusedLevels.typicalQuestion: How do I remove factor levels that no longer have any data after I filtered/subsetted my dataset?
dropUnusedLevels.mainAssumptions: The variable(s) are genuine factors with potentially unused levels
dropUnusedLevels.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s) with any unused (zero-observation) levels dropped.

inspectBoxCoxLambda.dialog: Lambda (λ) value for variables with prior Box-Cox transformation
inspectBoxCoxLambda.outcome: Displays the Box-Cox lambda currently stored for one or more variables.
inspectBoxCoxLambda.typicalQuestion: What Box-Cox lambda is currently stored for this variable?
inspectBoxCoxLambda.dataType: Variable(s) with a previously stored Box-Cox lambda
inspectBoxCoxLambda.mainAssumptions: A Box-Cox lambda has already been estimated/stored for the inspected variable(s)
inspectBoxCoxLambda.resultMeaning: A table of each variable's stored Box-Cox lambda.

inverseBoxCoxTransform.dialog: Inverse Box-Cox transformation (convert back to non-transformed value)
inverseBoxCoxTransform.outcome: Converts Box-Cox-transformed value(s) back to their original (non-transformed) scale, using a variable's stored or specified lambda.
inverseBoxCoxTransform.typicalQuestion: I have a Box-Cox transformed value - how do I convert it back to the original scale?
inverseBoxCoxTransform.dataType: A variable with stored (or manually specified) Box-Cox lambda
inverseBoxCoxTransform.mainAssumptions: The lambda used matches the one originally applied to the value(s)
inverseBoxCoxTransform.resultMeaning: The transformed value(s) converted back to their original, non-transformed scale.

labelNAasMissing.outcome: Assigns a display label (e.g. "Missing") to NA values within one or more factor variables.
labelNAasMissing.typicalQuestion: How do I give NA values in my factor variable a proper label like "Missing" instead of blank?
labelNAasMissing.resultMeaning: NA values in the selected factor variable(s) are relabeled with the specified label.

lumpIntoOther.dialog: Lump the least or most common factor levels
lumpIntoOther.outcome: Automatically collapses the least (or most) common levels of a factor variable into a single "Other" category, optionally weighted.
lumpIntoOther.typicalQuestion: How do I automatically combine rare factor levels into an "Other" category?
lumpIntoOther.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s) with sparse levels lumped into an "Other" category.

missValsFormula.outcome: Imputes missing values in a variable by predicting them from a user-specified regression formula involving other variables.
missValsFormula.typicalQuestion: How do I impute missing values in a variable using a regression formula based on other variables?
missValsFormula.dataType: A variable with missing values (dependent), predictor variables via formula
missValsFormula.mainAssumptions: The specified formula relationship reasonably predicts the missing values
missValsFormula.resultMeaning: The variable with missing values filled in using formula-based predictions.

missValsModelImputation.outcome: Imputes missing values in a variable using predictions from an already-specified/fitted predictive model.
missValsModelImputation.typicalQuestion: How do I impute missing values in a variable using a predictive model?
missValsModelImputation.dataType: A variable with missing values (dependent), model-based predictors
missValsModelImputation.mainAssumptions: The chosen model reasonably predicts the missing values
missValsModelImputation.resultMeaning: The variable with missing values filled in using model-based predictions.

missingValuesBasic.outcome: Replaces missing values in one or more numeric variables with a specified value or simple statistic (e.g. mean, median).
missingValuesBasic.typicalQuestion: How do I replace missing values in a numeric variable with the mean, median, or a fixed value?
missingValuesBasic.mainAssumptions: The chosen replacement (e.g. mean) is a reasonable stand-in for the missing values
missingValuesBasic.resultMeaning: The variable(s) with missing values replaced by the specified value/statistic.

nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.dialog: Box-Cox transformation of non normal data to normal
nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.outcome: Fits and applies a Box-Cox transformation to a non-normal variable, converting it toward approximate normality.
nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.typicalQuestion: My variable isn't normally distributed - how do I apply a Box-Cox transformation to normalize it?
nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.dataType: A non-normal numeric variable (positive values required)
nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.mainAssumptions: Values are positive; a power transformation can improve normality
nonNormalBoxCoxTransform.resultMeaning: A new (or overwritten) variable transformed to approximate normality, plus the fitted lambda.

rankVariables.outcome: Creates rank variables for one or more numeric variables, optionally computed within groups defined by another variable.
rankVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I rank a numeric variable's values, optionally within groups?
rankVariables.resultMeaning: New rank variable(s) for the selected numeric variable(s).

recodeVariables.outcome: Recodes values of one or more numeric, character, or factor variables according to specified old-value/new-value pairs, into new or existing variables.
recodeVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I recode specific values of a variable into different values (e.g. combining categories, relabeling codes)?
recodeVariables.mainAssumptions: None; a numeric variable stays numeric and a factor stays factor after recoding
recodeVariables.resultMeaning: The specified variable(s) recoded per the given old-value/new-value mapping, stored in new or overwritten variables.

removeNAs.outcome: Removes rows with missing (NA) values in one or more selected variables from the dataset.
removeNAs.typicalQuestion: How do I remove rows that have missing values in specific columns?
removeNAs.mainAssumptions: Complete-case analysis (dropping rows with any missing value in the selected variables) is acceptable
removeNAs.resultMeaning: The dataset with rows missing values in the selected variable(s) removed.

reorderByCount.outcome: Reorders a factor variable's levels by their observation count (frequency).
reorderByCount.typicalQuestion: How do I reorder a factor's levels by how frequently each occurs?
reorderByCount.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s)' levels reordered by frequency count.

reorderByOccurance.outcome: Reorders a factor variable's levels by the order in which they first appear in the dataset.
reorderByOccurance.typicalQuestion: How do I reorder a factor's levels by the order they first appear in my data?
reorderByOccurance.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s)' levels reordered by first-occurrence order.

replaceMissingValues.outcome: Replaces missing values in one or more string/factor variables with a specified replacement value/level.
replaceMissingValues.typicalQuestion: How do I replace missing values in a text/factor variable with a specific value?
replaceMissingValues.mainAssumptions: The chosen replacement value is a reasonable stand-in for the missing values
replaceMissingValues.resultMeaning: The variable(s) with missing values replaced by the specified value/level.

specifyLevelsToKeepOrReplace.dialog: Specify levels to keep or replace by other
specifyLevelsToKeepOrReplace.outcome: Manually specifies which factor levels to keep as-is and which to collapse into an "Other" category.
specifyLevelsToKeepOrReplace.typicalQuestion: How do I manually choose which factor levels to keep and which to lump into "Other"?
specifyLevelsToKeepOrReplace.resultMeaning: The factor variable(s) with the specified levels kept and the rest collapsed into "Other".

standardizeVariables.outcome: Standardizes one or more numeric variables (e.g. to mean 0, SD 1 - a z-score).
standardizeVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I standardize/z-score a numeric variable?

transformVariables.outcome: Applies a standard mathematical transformation (e.g. log, square root, inverse) to one or more numeric variables.
transformVariables.typicalQuestion: How do I apply a log, square-root, or other standard transformation to a numeric variable?
transformVariables.mainAssumptions: The chosen transformation is appropriate for the variable's range (e.g. log requires positive values)
